title.zh: 卷六十九 列傳第二十九 劉湛 范曄
title.en: Volume 69 Biographies 29: Liu Zhan, Fan Ye
title.raw: 卷六十九 列傳第二十九 劉湛 范曄 Volume 69 Biographies 29: Liu Zhan, Fan Ye

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十九 劉湛 范曄

translations.literal: Biographies 29: Liu Zhan, Fan Ye
translations.idiomatic: Biography 29: Liu Zhan and Fan Ye

sentences.zh: 劉湛，字弘仁，南陽涅陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan, styled Hongren, was a man of Nieyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan, courtesy name Hongren, was a native of Nieyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖耽，父柳，竝晉左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His grandfather Liu Dan (耽) and his father Liu (柳) both were Jin Left Grand Master of Splendid Hall and Commissioners with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liu Dan (耽) and his father Liu (柳) had both held Jin offices as Left Grand Master of Splendid Hall and as Commissioners with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 湛出繼伯父淡，襲封安眾縣五等男。

translations.literal: Zhan was given in adoption to his uncle Liu Dan (淡) and inherited enfeoffment as fifth-grade Marquis of Anzhong County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was adopted out to his uncle Liu Dan (淡) and succeeded to the fifth-grade marquisate of Anzhong County.

sentences.zh: 少有局力，不尚浮華。

translations.literal: In youth he had breadth and force, and did not esteem flashy display.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed breadth of mind and force of character, and he did not care for flashy display.

sentences.zh: 博涉史傳，諳前世舊典，弱年便有宰世情，常自比管夷吾、諸葛亮，不為文章，不喜談議。

translations.literal: He broadly traversed histories and traditions, was versed in former-age old statutes, in weak years already had the sentiment of ruling the age, often compared himself to Guan Yiwu and Zhuge Liang, did not compose literary pieces, and did not enjoy talk and discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in histories and chronicles and knew the statutes of earlier ages by heart; even in his youth he harbored ambitions to govern the realm and often likened himself to Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang. He did not write belles lettres and disliked idle talk.

sentences.zh: 本州辟主簿，不就。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as Registrar, and he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the province summoned him as Registrar, he declined the post.

sentences.zh: 除著作佐郎，又不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library, and again did not accept the seal.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library but again refused to take office.

sentences.zh: 高祖以為太尉行參軍，賞遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu made him Acting Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant, and rewarded and treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu appointed him Acting Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant and treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 高祖領鎮西將軍、荊州刺史，以湛為功曹，仍補治中別駕從事史，復為太尉參軍，世子征虜西中郎主簿。

translations.literal: When Gaozu held the posts of General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Jing Province, he made Zhan Merit Officer, then also supplemented him as Registrar of the Headquarters, Separate-Chariot Master of Records, and Attending Clerk, again as Grand Commandant Staff Officer, and as Registrar to the Heir Apparent, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, Western Center-Rank Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu served as General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Jing Province, he appointed Zhan Merit Officer, then also made him Registrar of the Headquarters, Separate-Chariot Master of Records, and Attending Clerk; Zhan later served again as Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant and as Registrar to the heir apparent, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, Western Center-Rank Commandant.

sentences.zh: 父柳亡於江州，州府送故甚豐，一無所受，時論稱之。

translations.literal: When his father Liu (柳) died in Jiang Province, the province and prefecture sent funeral goods in great abundance, and he accepted none of it; opinion of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Liu (柳) died in Jiang Province, the provincial and prefectural offices sent lavish funeral gifts, but he accepted none of them, and contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 服終，除秘書丞，出為相國參軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed Palace Library Assistant and went out as Staff Officer to the Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he was appointed Assistant Director of the Palace Library and then sent out as Staff Officer to the Chancellor of State.

sentences.zh: 謝晦、王弘並稱其有器幹。

translations.literal: Xie Hui and Wang Hong both praised him as having capacity and backbone.
translations.idiomatic: Both Xie Hui and Wang Hong praised him for his talent and force of character.

sentences.zh: 高祖入受晉命，以第四子義康為冠軍將軍、豫州刺史，留鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered and received the Jin mandate, he made his fourth son Yikang General Who Conquers Champions and Governor of Yu Province, leaving him to garrison Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu accepted the Jin mandate and took the throne, he appointed his fourth son Yikang General Who Conquers Champions and Governor of Yu Province and left him to garrison Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 以湛為長史、梁郡太守。

translations.literal: He made Zhan Chief Clerk and Grand Administrator of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zhan Chief Clerk and Grand Administrator of Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 義康弱年未親政，府州軍事悉委湛。

translations.literal: Yikang was young and had not personally taken government; all military affairs of the prefecture and province were entrusted to Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang was still young and did not administer affairs himself; Zhan was entrusted with all military affairs of the prefecture and province.

sentences.zh: 府進號右將軍，仍隨府轉。

translations.literal: The headquarters advanced in title to General of the Right, and he still followed the headquarters in transfer.
translations.idiomatic: When the headquarters was promoted to General of the Right, Zhan transferred with it as before.

sentences.zh: 義康以本號徙為南豫州，湛改領歷陽太守。

translations.literal: Yikang was moved on his original title to Southern Yu Province, and Zhan changed to hold concurrently the Grand Administrator of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang was transferred to Southern Yu Province under his existing title, Zhan was reassigned to serve concurrently as Grand Administrator of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 為人剛嚴用法，奸吏犯贓百錢以上，皆殺之，自下莫不震肅。

translations.literal: As a man he was stern and strict in applying the law; corrupt officials who violated bribery for a hundred cash or more were all put to death, and from below none did not tremble into order.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern and rigorous in enforcing the law: any corrupt official guilty of embezzling as little as a hundred cash was executed, and everyone below him was awed into discipline.

sentences.zh: 廬陵王義真出為車騎將軍、南豫州刺史，湛又為長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: Prince of Luling Yizhen went out as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Southern Yu Province; Zhan again served as Chief Clerk, Grand Administrator as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Luling Yizhen was sent out as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Southern Yu Province, Zhan again became his Chief Clerk while retaining his post as Grand Administrator.

sentences.zh: 義真時居高祖憂，使帳下備膳，湛禁之，義真乃使左右索魚肉珍羞，於齋內別立廚帳。

translations.literal: Yizhen was then in Gaozu's mourning, and had his attendants prepare meals; Zhan forbade it, so Yizhen had his attendants seek fish, meat, and delicacies and separately set up a kitchen tent within the mourning quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was then observing mourning for Gaozu and had his attendants prepare meals, but Zhan forbade it; Yizhen then had his men procure fish, meat, and delicacies and set up a separate kitchen tent within the mourning compound.

sentences.zh: 會湛入，因命臑酒炙車螯，湛正色曰：「公當今不宜有此設。」

translations.literal: When Zhan entered, he thereupon ordered cured meat, wine, roast, and chariot-claw [crab]; Zhan with stern countenance said: "Your Highness at present ought not have this spread."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan came in, Yizhen ordered cured meats, wine, roast crab, and other delicacies. Zhan said sternly, "Your Highness ought not have such provisions at a time like this."

sentences.zh: 義真曰：「旦甚寒，一碗酒亦何傷！

translations.literal: Yizhen said: "The morning is very cold—what harm is one bowl of wine!
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen replied, "The mornings are bitterly cold—what harm can there be in a single bowl of wine?

sentences.zh: 長史事同一家，望不為異。」

translations.literal: The Chief Clerk's affairs are the same as one family—I hope you will not regard it as strange."
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Clerk and I are as one household; I hope you will not take exception."

sentences.zh: 酒既至，湛因起曰：「既不能以禮自處，又不能以禮處人。」

translations.literal: When the wine had arrived, Zhan thereupon rose and said: "You can neither conduct yourself by ritual, nor treat others by ritual."
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was served, Zhan rose and said, "You cannot keep ritual discipline yourself, and you cannot treat others with ritual propriety either."

sentences.zh: 景平元年，召入，拜尚書吏部郎，遷右衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingping, he was summoned to court, appointed personnel bureau director in the Department of State Affairs, and transferred to general of the right guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingping, he was summoned to court, appointed personnel bureau director in the Department of State Affairs, and transferred to general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 出督廣、交二州諸軍事、建威將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out to command all military affairs of Guang and Jiao provinces, as general who establishes authority, general of the palace gentlemen who pacifies Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to command military affairs in Guang and Jiao provinces, serving as general who establishes authority, general of the palace gentlemen who pacifies Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 嫡母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office because of mourning for his principal mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his principal mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為侍中。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed, he became palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning was completed, he became palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 撫軍將軍江夏王義恭鎮江陵，以湛為使持節、南蠻校尉、領撫軍長史，行府州事。

translations.literal: When Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia and general who pacifies the army, garrisoned Jiangling, he made Zhan envoy holding the tally, colonel of the Southern Man, concurrently chief clerk to the general who pacifies the army, and acting administrator of the affairs of the headquarters and province.
translations.idiomatic: When Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia and general who pacifies the army, garrisoned Jiangling, he made Zhan envoy holding the tally, colonel of the Southern Man, concurrently chief clerk to the general who pacifies the army, with acting authority over headquarters and provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 時王弘輔政，而王華、王曇首任事居中，湛自謂才能不後之，不願外出；

translations.literal: At that time Wang Hong assisted in government, while Wang Hua and Wang Tanshou held responsibility for affairs at court. Zhan considered his talents no lower than theirs and did not wish to go out to the provinces;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Hong assisted in government, while Wang Hua and Wang Tanshou held office at court. Zhan considered his talents no less than theirs and did not wish to be sent out;

sentences.zh: 是行也，謂為弘等所斥，意甚不平，常曰：「二王若非代邸之舊，無以至此，可謂遭遇風雲。」

translations.literal: Regarding this posting, he thought he had been pushed out by Hong and the others, and his mind was very resentful. He often said, "If the two Wangs were not old associates from the princely residence, they would have had no way to reach this. One may say they met the winds and clouds."
translations.idiomatic: He believed this appointment meant that Hong and the others had pushed him aside and was deeply resentful. He often said, "Had the two Wangs not been old associates from the princely residence, they could never have reached such positions. They truly met their wind and clouds."

sentences.zh: 湛負其志氣，常慕汲黯、崔琰為人，故名長子曰黯字長孺，第二子曰琰字季珪。

translations.literal: Zhan relied on his will and spirit, often admired Ji An and Cui Yan as men, and therefore named his eldest son An, styled Changru, and his second son Yan, styled Jigui.
translations.idiomatic: Proud of his own spirit, Zhan often admired the examples of Ji An and Cui Yan; he therefore named his eldest son An, courtesy name Changru, and his second son Yan, courtesy name Jigui.

sentences.zh: 琰於江陵病卒，湛求自送喪還都，義恭亦為之陳請。

translations.literal: Yan died of illness at Jiangling; Zhan requested to escort the coffin himself back to the capital, and Yigong also submitted a petition on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan died of illness at Jiangling, Zhan asked permission to escort the coffin back to the capital himself, and Yigong also petitioned on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 太祖答義恭曰：「吾亦得湛啟事，為之酸懷，乃不欲苟違所請。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu replied to Yigong: "I too have received Zhan's memorial; I am sore at heart for him and do not wish lightly to go against what he asks.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu replied to Yigong, "I too have received Zhan's memorial, and it pains me; I do not wish lightly to refuse his request.

sentences.zh: 但汝弱年，新涉庶務，八州殷曠，專斷事重，疇諮委仗，不可不得其人，量算二三，未獲便相順許。

translations.literal: But you are in weak years, newly entering the multitude of affairs; the eight provinces are vast and populous, and exclusive decision on affairs is weighty—whom to consult and entrust cannot be without the right man; I have reckoned two or three times and have not yet been able readily to grant assent.
translations.idiomatic: But you are still young and have only lately taken up civil administration; the eight provinces are vast and populous, and the power to decide affairs on your own is a heavy burden. I cannot do without the right man to advise and rely upon you. I have weighed the matter again and again and cannot yet readily grant your request.

sentences.zh: 今答湛啟，權停彼葬。

translations.literal: Now in answering Zhan's memorial, I provisionally halt the burial there.
translations.idiomatic: In my reply to Zhan's memorial I have provisionally deferred the burial there.

sentences.zh: 頃朝臣零落相係，寄懷轉寡，湛實國器，吾乃欲引其令還，直以西夏任重，要且停此事耳。

translations.literal: Recently court ministers have fallen away one after another, and those in whom I place my hopes grow fewer; Zhan is truly a vessel of state—I wish to summon him back, but simply because the western region's burden is heavy, for now I must halt this matter.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers have been dying off one after another, and I have fewer men in whom I can place my hopes. Zhan is truly a pillar of the state, and I had intended to recall him—but the western command is too weighty a responsibility, so for now I must put off this matter.

sentences.zh: 汝慶賞黜罰，豫關失得者，必宜悉相委寄。」

translations.literal: Your rewards, promotions, dismissals, and punishments that bear on gain and loss—you must wholly entrust them to him."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever concerns rewards, promotions, dismissals, and punishments that touch upon success or failure, you must entrust entirely to him."

sentences.zh: 義恭性甚狷隘，年又漸長，欲專政事，每為湛所裁，主佐之間，嫌隙遂構。

translations.literal: Yigong's nature was very narrow and cramped; his years gradually grew, and he wished to monopolize government affairs, but was each time checked by Zhan—between lord and aide, resentment and rifts thus formed.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong was narrow-minded by nature, and as he grew older he wished to monopolize administrative affairs, but Zhan repeatedly checked him; resentment thus grew between prince and chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，密遣使詰讓義恭，并使深加諧緝。

translations.literal: When Taizu heard of it, he secretly sent an envoy to rebuke Yigong and also had him deepen harmony and binding.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu heard of this, he secretly sent an envoy to rebuke Yigong and ordered him to restore harmony with Zhan.

sentences.zh: 義恭具陳湛無居下之禮，又自以年長，未得行意，雖奉詔旨，頗有怨言。

translations.literal: Yigong fully set forth that Zhan lacked the ritual of one who dwells below, and also considered himself older and unable to carry out his intent; though he received the imperial order, he had considerable words of complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong detailed how Zhan failed to observe the deference owed by a subordinate, and complained that, though he was the elder, he could not have his way; despite obeying the imperial order, he harbored considerable resentment.

sentences.zh: 上友于素篤，欲加酬順，乃詔之曰：「事至於此，甚為可歎。

translations.literal: The Emperor's brotherly affection had always been deep, and he wished to add repayment and compliance; he therefore issued an edict to him: "Matters have come to this—it is greatly lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had always been deeply affectionate toward his brothers and wished to placate Yigong, so he issued an edict saying, "Matters have come to this point—it is deeply regrettable.

sentences.zh: 當今乏才，委授已爾，宜盡相彌縫，取其可取，棄其可棄。

translations.literal: At present talent is scarce; the commission is already thus—you ought fully to patch and seam together, take what can be taken, discard what can be discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Talent is scarce today, and the appointment has already been made; you should do your utmost to smooth things over, accept what is acceptable in him, and overlook what must be overlooked.

sentences.zh: 汝疏云『泯然無際』，如此甚佳。

translations.literal: Your memorial says 'blended without boundary'—this is very good.
translations.idiomatic: In your memorial you wrote that you would be 'utterly without boundary' with him—that is excellent."

sentences.zh: 彼多猜，不可令萬一覺也。

translations.literal: He is much given to suspicion—you must not let him perceive it in the slightest.
translations.idiomatic: He is suspicious by nature; you must not let him notice the slightest hint of it.

sentences.zh: 汝年已長，漸更事物，且群情矚望，不以幼昧相期，何由故如十歲時，動止諮問。

translations.literal: Your years are already grown; you gradually change in affairs, and moreover the multitude's feelings gaze upon you—they do not expect childish obscurity from you; how can you still be as at age ten, consulting on every movement and rest?
translations.idiomatic: You are grown now and should gradually take charge of affairs; everyone looks to you and no longer expects childish inexperience. Why should you still consult on every move as you did at age ten?

sentences.zh: 但當今所專，必是小事耳。

translations.literal: But what you monopolize at present must surely be small matters.
translations.idiomatic: But whatever you insist on controlling now must surely be minor matters.

sentences.zh: 亦恐量此輕重，未必盡得，彼之疑怨，兼或由此邪？」

translations.literal: I also fear that in weighing this light and heavy you may not fully attain it—might his suspicion and resentment partly arise from this?"
translations.idiomatic: I also fear you may not judge such matters correctly, and that his suspicion and resentment may partly stem from this."

sentences.zh: 先是，王華既亡，曇首又卒，領軍將軍殷景仁以時賢零落，白太祖徴湛。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Wang Hua had died and Tanshou also passed away, General of the Palace Guard Yin Jingren, because the worthies of the time were falling away, reported to Taizu to summon Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Wang Hua died and Xu Tanshou passed away as well, General of the Palace Guard Yin Jingren, seeing that talented men were dying off, reported to Taizu recommending that Zhan be summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 八年，召為太子詹事，加給事中、本州大中正，與景仁竝被任遇。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Zhan was summoned as Household Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with additional posts as Attendant Within the Gates and Grand Rectifier of his native province; Zhan and Jingren were both favored in appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Zhan was summoned to serve as Household Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with additional appointments as Attendant Within the Gates and Grand Rectifier of his native province; Zhan and Jingren were both favored at court.

sentences.zh: 湛常云：「今世宰相何難，此政可當我南陽郡漢世功曹耳。」

translations.literal: Zhan often said: "What difficulty is there in being chancellor of this age? This is just fit to be my Nanyang commandery Han-era Merit Officer."
translations.idiomatic: Zhan often said, "What difficulty is there in being chancellor today? The post is no more demanding than the Merit Officer of Nanyang Commandery in Han times."

sentences.zh: 明年，景仁轉尚書僕射、領選、護軍將軍，湛代為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: The next year Jingren transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, holding selection duties and as General Who Protects the Army; Zhan replaced him as General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jingren was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, with charge of personnel selection, and appointed General Who Protects the Army; Zhan replaced him as General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 十二年，又領詹事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he also held concurrently the Household Mentor post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he also held the post of Household Mentor concurrently.

sentences.zh: 湛與景仁素款，又以其建議徴之，甚相感說。

translations.literal: Zhan and Jingren had long been on intimate terms, and moreover because the latter had recommended summoning him, they were deeply moved and pleased with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan and Jingren had long been on friendly terms, and Zhan was deeply grateful because Jingren had recommended his summons to court.

sentences.zh: 及俱被時遇，猜隙漸生，以景仁專管內任，謂為間己。

translations.literal: When both were favored by the times, suspicion and rifts gradually arose; because Jingren exclusively managed inner duties, Zhan took it as coming between himself and the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Once both were favored at court, suspicion gradually arose between them; Zhan resented that Jingren monopolized inner-court affairs and saw this as an attempt to shut him out.

sentences.zh: 時彭城王義康專秉朝權，而湛昔為上佐，遂以舊情委心自結，欲因宰相之力以回主心，傾黜景仁，獨當時務。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Pengcheng Yikang monopolized court power, and Zhan had formerly been his chief aide; he therefore entrusted his heart and bound himself through old affection, wishing by the chancellor's strength to turn the ruler's mind, topple and dismiss Jingren, and alone handle the affairs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince of Pengcheng Yikang monopolized court power. Zhan, who had once served as his chief aide, entrusted himself to Yikang out of old affection, hoping to use the prince's power to sway the emperor, bring down Jingren, and handle state affairs alone.

sentences.zh: 義康屢構之於太祖，其事不行。

translations.literal: Yikang repeatedly framed charges against him to Taizu, but the matter did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang repeatedly slandered Jingren to Taizu, but the effort failed.

sentences.zh: 義康僚屬及湛諸附隸潛相約勒，無敢歷殷氏門者。

translations.literal: Yikang's staff and all Zhan's attached followers secretly bound one another by covenant—none dared to pass through the Yin clan's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang's staff and all of Zhan's followers secretly agreed among themselves that none would dare visit the Yin household.

sentences.zh: 湛黨劉敬文父成未悟其機，詣景仁求郡，敬文遽往謝湛曰：「老父悖耄，遂就殷鐵干祿。

translations.literal: Zhan's partisan Liu Jingwen's father Cheng had not grasped the scheme and went to Jingren to seek a commandery; Jingwen hastened to apologize to Zhan, saying: "My old father is perverse and senile and has gone to Yin Tie, that is, Yin Jingren, to seek salary.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cheng, father of Zhan's follower Liu Jingwen, failed to grasp the situation and went to Jingren to request a commandery appointment. Jingwen hurried to apologize to Zhan, saying, "My old father is senile and has gone to Yin Tie, that is, Yin Jingren, to seek an office for profit.

sentences.zh: 由敬文闇淺，上負生成，合門慚懼，無地自處。」

translations.literal: Because Jingwen is dark and shallow, above he has failed the life-giving favor—our whole house is ashamed and afraid, with no place to set ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: It is because Jingwen is obtuse and shallow that he has failed you who gave us life; our whole family is ashamed and afraid, with nowhere to hide our faces."

sentences.zh: 敬文之姦諂無愧如此。

translations.literal: Jingwen's treacherous flattery was shameless to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the shameless treachery and flattery of Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 義康擅勢專朝，威傾內外，湛愈推崇之，無復人臣之禮，上稍不能平。

translations.literal: Yikang usurped power and monopolized the court; his authority leaned upon inner and outer alike. Zhan increasingly exalted him, no longer observing a minister's ritual, and the Emperor gradually could not be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang usurped power and dominated the court, his authority overwhelming both court and realm. Zhan flattered him ever more extravagantly and no longer observed the deference owed by a subject, and the emperor grew increasingly displeased.

sentences.zh: 湛初入朝，委任甚重，日夕引接，恩禮綢繆。

translations.literal: When Zhan first entered the court, his commission was very weighty; morning and evening he was summoned and received, favor and ritual thick and close.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan first came to court, he was entrusted with weighty responsibilities; the emperor received him morning and evening with thick favor and courtesy.

sentences.zh: 善論治道，並諳前世故事，敘致銓理，聽者忘疲。

translations.literal: He was skilled at discussing the way of governance and was also versed in former-age precedents; in narration and arrangement he weighed and ordered matters, and listeners forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at discussing statecraft and knew the precedents of earlier ages by heart; his discourse was orderly and well weighed, and listeners forgot their fatigue.

sentences.zh: 每入雲龍門，御者便解駕，左右及羽儀隨意分散，不夕不出，以此為常。

translations.literal: Each time Zhan entered Cloud-Dragon Gate, the imperial driver at once unyoked the carriage; attendants left and right and ceremonial guards dispersed as they pleased—Zhan did not leave before evening; this became his constant.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhan entered the Cloud-Dragon Gate, the imperial driver would unhitch the carriage; attendants and ceremonial guards would disperse at will, and Zhan would not leave until evening—this became his routine.

sentences.zh: 及至晚節，驅煽義康，凌轢朝廷，上意雖內離，而接遇不改。

translations.literal: When it came to his later years, he drove and fanned Yikang, overbearing upon the court; though the Emperor's mind inwardly parted from him, his reception and treatment did not change.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he incited Yikang and rode roughshod over the court. Though the emperor inwardly turned against him, his outward treatment of Zhan did not change.

sentences.zh: 上嘗謂所親曰：「劉班初自西還，吾與語，常看日早晚，慮其當去。

translations.literal: The Emperor once said to those close to him: "When Liu Zhan, whom I called Ban, first returned from the west, when I spoke with him I always watched whether the day was early or late, fearing he would leave.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to his intimates, "When Liu Zhan, whom I called Ban, first returned from the west, whenever I talked with him I kept watching the sun, afraid he would leave.

sentences.zh: 比入，吾亦看日早晚，慮其不去。」

translations.literal: Now when he comes in, I also watch whether the day is early or late, fearing he will not leave."
translations.idiomatic: But now when he comes in, I still watch the sun—afraid he will not leave."

sentences.zh: 湛小字班虎，故云班也。

translations.literal: Zhan's childhood name was Banhu, hence he is called Ban.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's childhood name was Banhu, hence the emperor called him Ban.

sentences.zh: 遷丹陽尹，金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，詹事如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Intendant of Danyang, Grand Master of Splendid Hall with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with additional post as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Household Mentor as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Intendant of Danyang, appointed Grand Master of Splendid Hall with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and given the additional post of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry while retaining his position as Household Mentor.

sentences.zh: 十七年，所生母亡。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Zhan's birth mother died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Zhan's birth mother died.

sentences.zh: 時上與義康形跡既乖，釁難將結，湛亦知無復全地。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor and Yikang's outward traces had already parted, and trouble was about to bind; Zhan also knew there was no longer any ground for preservation.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor and Yikang had already grown estranged, and disaster was imminent; Zhan too knew he could no longer survive unscathed.

sentences.zh: 及至丁艱，謂所親曰：「今年必敗。

translations.literal: When Zhan entered mourning for his parent, he said to those close to him: "This year I am sure to be ruined.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan entered mourning, he told his intimates, "This year I am sure to be ruined.

sentences.zh: 常日正賴口舌爭之，故得推遷耳。

translations.literal: On ordinary days I just relied on tongue and mouth to contend—that is why I could be put off.
translations.idiomatic: On ordinary days I could still argue my case in person and so win delays.

sentences.zh: 今既窮毒，無復此望，禍至其能久乎！」

translations.literal: Now I am already cornered in poison, and have no more this hope—when disaster comes, how can it long endure!"
translations.idiomatic: Now I am utterly cornered and have no such hope left—when disaster strikes, how long can it be delayed?"

sentences.zh: 十月，詔曰：「劉湛階藉門廕，少叨榮位，往佐歷陽，姧詖夙著。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict said: "Liu Zhan, relying on his family's rank and shade, in youth usurped honored position; formerly assisting at Liyang, treachery and perversity were long manifest.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an edict declared, "Liu Zhan, relying on his family's rank and privilege, early gained honored office; when he formerly served at Liyang, his treachery and perversity were already well known.

sentences.zh: 謝晦之難，潛使密告，求心即事，久宜誅屏。

translations.literal: In Xie Hui's crisis he secretly sent secret reports, seeking the heart and taking the matter at once—long ago he ought to have been executed and removed.
translations.idiomatic: During Xie Hui's rebellion he secretly sent reports; he sought favor by seizing the moment and long ago deserved execution and removal.

sentences.zh: 朕所以棄罪略瑕，庶收後效，寵秩優忝，踰越倫匹。

translations.literal: We therefore set aside guilt and passed over flaws, hoping to gather later effect; favored rank was generous beyond desert, exceeding peers in order.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore overlooked his crimes and flaws, hoping he would prove useful later; we favored him with rank beyond his desert, exceeding what his peers received.

sentences.zh: 而凶忍忌克，剛愎靡厭，無君之心，觸遇斯發。

translations.literal: Yet he was fierce, cruel, jealous, and overbearing, stubborn and self-willed without satiety, with a heart lacking a ruler—when touched he at once erupted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was fierce, cruel, jealous, and overbearing, stubborn and insatiable, with a heart that lacked loyalty to his ruler—he erupted at the slightest provocation.

sentences.zh: 遂乃合黨連群，構扇同異，附下蔽上，專弄威權，薦子樹親，互為表裏，邪附者榮曜九族，乘理者推陷必至。

translations.literal: He then formed factions and linked cliques, framed and fanned dissension, attached to those below and screened those above, monopolized and played with authority, recommended sons and planted kin, mutually inner and outer—those who adhered in evil had their nine clans glorified in splendor; those who seized upon principle were pushed into traps without fail.
translations.idiomatic: He formed factions and stirred up discord, curried favor below while deceiving those above, and monopolized power; he promoted his sons and planted his kin as mutual insiders and outsiders—those who joined him in evil saw their whole clans glorified, while those who stood on principle were inevitably destroyed.

sentences.zh: 旋觀姧慝，為日已久，猶欲弘納遵養，冀或悛革。

translations.literal: Looking back upon treacherous evil, the days have been long; we still wished broadly to accept and follow in nurturing him, hoping perhaps he would reform.
translations.idiomatic: We have long observed his treacherous wickedness, yet still wished to embrace and nurture him, hoping he might reform.

sentences.zh: 自邇以來，凌縱滋甚，悖言懟容，罔所顧忌，險謀潛計，睥睨兩宮。

translations.literal: From recent times his overbearing license has grown ever worse; rebellious words and defiant countenance, with nothing heeded in restraint; treacherous plots and hidden schemes, glaring sidelong at the two palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Recently his arrogance has grown ever worse; his rebellious words and defiant bearing show no restraint; his treacherous plots and secret schemes cast a sidelong eye upon both palaces.

sentences.zh: 豈唯彰暴國都，固亦達于四海。

translations.literal: How could it be only that violence is displayed in the capital—it indeed reaches to the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: His outrages are manifest not only in the capital but reach to the four seas.

sentences.zh: 比年七曜違度，震蝕表災，侵陽之徵，事符幽顯。

translations.literal: In recent years the seven luminaries have violated their degrees; earthquakes and eclipses display calamity; signs of encroaching upon yang—the matter accords with hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the seven luminaries have strayed from their courses; earthquakes and eclipses have proclaimed disaster—signs of encroachment upon the yang principle, matching what is hidden and what is manifest.

sentences.zh: 搢紳含憤，義夫興歎。

translations.literal: Girdled officials harbor anger; men of righteousness raise sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Officials harbor indignation, and men of righteousness sigh in dismay.

sentences.zh: 昔齊、魯不綱，禍傾邦國；

translations.literal: Formerly, when Qi and Lu lacked order, disaster overturned their states;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when Qi and Lu fell out of order, disaster overturned their states;

sentences.zh: 昭、宣電斷，漢祚方延。

translations.literal: when Zhao and Xuan cut off like lightning, Han's mandate was then extended.
translations.idiomatic: when Emperors Zhao and Xuan acted with lightning decisiveness, the Han mandate was thereby prolonged.

sentences.zh: 便收付廷尉，肅明刑典。」

translations.literal: Let him at once be taken and delivered to the Minister of Justice, to make solemn and clear the penal statutes."
translations.idiomatic: He is therefore to be handed over to the Minister of Justice so that the penal code may be solemnly enforced."

sentences.zh: 於獄伏誅，時年四十九。

translations.literal: In prison he submitted to execution; he was then forty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed in prison at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子黯，大將軍從事中郎。

translations.literal: His son An was Attending Clerk to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: His son An served as Attending Clerk to the Grand General.

sentences.zh: 黯及二弟亮、儼並從誅。

translations.literal: An and his two younger brothers Liang and Yan were all executed along with him.
translations.idiomatic: An and his two younger brothers Liang and Yan were all executed with him.

sentences.zh: 湛弟素，黃門侍郎，徙廣州。

translations.literal: Zhan's younger brother Su was Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and was banished to Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's younger brother Su, a Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate, was banished to Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 湛初被收，歎曰：「便是亂邪。」

translations.literal: When Zhan was first taken into custody, he sighed and said: "So it is disorder after all."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan was first arrested, he sighed and said, "So there will be disorder after all."

sentences.zh: 仍又曰：「不言無我應亂，殺我自是亂法耳。」

translations.literal: He then also said: "It is not to say that without me there ought to be disorder—killing me is itself disordering the law."
translations.idiomatic: He then added, "It is not that disorder would not occur without me—but killing me is itself a violation of proper law."

sentences.zh: 入獄見素，曰：「乃復及汝邪？

translations.literal: Entering prison he saw Su and said: "So it has reached even you?
translations.idiomatic: When he entered prison and saw Su, he said, "So it has reached even you?

sentences.zh: 相勸為惡，惡不可為；

translations.literal: We urged one another to do evil—evil cannot be done;
translations.idiomatic: We urged one another to do evil, yet evil ought not to be done;

sentences.zh: 相勸為善，正見今日。

translations.literal: we urged one another to do good—and just look at today.
translations.idiomatic: we urged one another to do good—and just look at us today.

sentences.zh: 如何！」

translations.literal: What of it!"
translations.idiomatic: What then!"

sentences.zh: 湛生女輒殺之，為士流所怪。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhan fathered a daughter he at once killed her, which the gentry stream found strange.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan killed every daughter born to him, which the gentry found shocking.

sentences.zh: 范曄，字蔚宗，順陽人，車騎將軍泰少子也。

translations.literal: Fan Ye, styled Weizong, was a man of Shunyang, the youngest son of General of Chariots and Cavalry Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye, courtesy name Weizong, was a native of Shunyang and the youngest son of General of Chariots and Cavalry Fan Tai.

sentences.zh: 母如廁產之，額為磚所傷，故以磚為小字。

translations.literal: His mother bore him in the privy; his forehead was injured by a brick, and therefore Zhuan, meaning "Brick," was made his childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: His mother gave birth to him in a privy; his forehead was struck by a brick, and therefore Zhuan, meaning "Brick," became his childhood name.

sentences.zh: 出繼從伯弘之，襲封武興縣五等侯。

translations.literal: He was given in adoption to his father's younger cousin Hongzhi and inherited enfeoffment as fifth-grade Marquis of Wuxing County.
translations.idiomatic: He was adopted out to his father's younger cousin Hongzhi and succeeded to the fifth-grade marquisate of Wuxing County.

sentences.zh: 少好學，博涉經史，善為文章，能隸書，曉音律。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, broadly traversed the classics and histories, was skilled at composing literary pieces, could write clerical script, and understood pitch and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and read widely in the classics and histories; he was skilled at literary composition, could write clerical script, and understood music and pitch.

sentences.zh: 年十七，州辟主簿，不就。

translations.literal: At age seventeen the province summoned him as Registrar, and he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen the province summoned him as Registrar, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 高祖相國掾，彭城王義康冠軍參軍，隨府轉右軍參軍，入補尚書外兵郎，出為荊州別駕從事史。

translations.literal: He was Staff Member to Gaozu's Chancellor of State, Staff Officer to Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, General Who Conquers Champions; he followed the headquarters in transfer to Staff Officer to the General of the Right, entered to fill the post of Outer Troops Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and went out as Separate-Chariot Attending Clerk of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Staff Member to Emperor Gaozu when the latter was Chancellor of State, then as Staff Officer to Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, General Who Conquers Champions; he transferred with the prince's staff to Staff Officer to the General of the Right, entered court as Outer Troops Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and was sent out as Separate-Chariot Attending Clerk of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 尋召為秘書丞，父憂去職。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Assistant Director of the Palace Library; on his father's mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to serve as Assistant Director of the Palace Library but left office upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 服終，為征南大將軍檀道濟司馬，領新蔡太守。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he served as Major to General Who Conquers the South Tan Daoji, holding concurrently the Grand Administrator of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he served as Major to General Who Conquers the South Tan Daoji and concurrently as Grand Administrator of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 道濟北征，曄憚行，辭以腳疾，上不許，使由水道統載器仗部伍。

translations.literal: When Daoji campaigned north, Ye feared going and declined on grounds of foot ailment; the Emperor did not permit it and had him by waterway oversee loading of weapons, gear, and troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoji marched north, Ye dreaded the campaign and pleaded foot ailment; the emperor refused and ordered him to travel by waterway to oversee the transport of weapons, equipment, and troops.

sentences.zh: 軍還，為司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he became Attending Clerk to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he was appointed Attending Clerk to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was transferred to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing in charge of personnel.

sentences.zh: 元嘉元年冬，彭城太妃薨，將葬，祖夕，僚故並集東府。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Yuanjia, the Grand Consort of Pengcheng died; when she was about to be buried, on the eve of the ancestral farewell, officials and former associates all gathered at the Eastern Residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Yuanjia, the Grand Consort of Pengcheng died. As her burial approached, officials and old associates gathered at the Eastern Residence on the eve of the farewell rites.

sentences.zh: 曄弟廣淵，時為司徒祭酒，其日在直。

translations.literal: Ye's younger brother Guangyuan was then Libationer to the Minister of Education, and on that day he was on duty.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's younger brother Guangyuan was then serving as Libationer to the Minister of Education and was on duty that day.

sentences.zh: 曄與司徒左西屬王深宿廣淵許，夜中酣飲，開北牖聽挽歌為樂。

translations.literal: Ye and Wang Shen, Left Western Subordinate of the Minister of Education, lodged at Guangyuan's place; in the middle of the night they drank heavily, opened the northern window, and took pleasure in listening to the funeral dirges.
translations.idiomatic: Ye and Wang Shen, the Minister of Education's Left Western Subordinate, stayed at Guangyuan's quarters. Deep in the night they drank to excess, opened the north window, and amused themselves by listening to the funeral dirges.

sentences.zh: 義康大怒，左遷曄宣城太守。

translations.literal: Yikang was greatly angered and demoted Ye to be Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang was furious and demoted Ye to Administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 不得志，乃刪眾家後漢書為一家之作。

translations.literal: Unable to realize his ambitions, he then edited the many schools' Books of the Later Han into the work of a single school.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated in office, he edited the various existing histories of the Later Han into a single work.

sentences.zh: 在郡數年，遷長沙王義欣鎮軍長史，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: After several years in the commandery, he was transferred to be Senior Clerk of the Army of Yixin, Prince of Changsha, and was additionally made General Pacifying the North.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in the commandery, he was transferred to serve as Senior Clerk of the Army for Yixin, Prince of Changsha, with the added title General Pacifying the North.

sentences.zh: 兄皓為宜都太守，嫡母隨皓在官。

translations.literal: His elder brother Hao was Administrator of Yidu, and his principal mother accompanied Hao at his office.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Hao was Administrator of Yidu, and his principal mother accompanied Hao to his post.

sentences.zh: 十六年，母亡，報之以疾，曄不時奔赴，及行，又攜妓妾自隨，為御史中丞劉損所奏，太祖愛其才，不罪也。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, his mother died; it had been reported to him as illness, but Ye did not hasten there in time, and when he went, he also took singing girls and concubines along with him; Liu Sun, Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief, memorialized against him, but Taizu loved his talent and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year his mother died. Although word of her illness had been sent to him, Ye did not hurry home in time, and when he finally set out he took singing girls and concubines with him. Liu Sun, Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief, impeached him, but Taizu valued his talent and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為始興王濬後軍長史，領南下邳太守。

translations.literal: When the mourning period was completed, he became Senior Clerk of the Rear Army of Jun, Prince of Shixing, and concurrently served as Administrator of Southern Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning, he became Senior Clerk of the Rear Army for Jun, Prince of Shixing, while concurrently serving as Administrator of Southern Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 及濬為揚州，未親政事，悉以委曄。

translations.literal: When Jun became governor of Yang Province, he had not yet personally handled affairs of government, and entrusted all of them to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun took charge of Yang Province, he was not yet personally managing government affairs and entrusted them all to Ye.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左衛將軍、太子詹事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Guard General and Household Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to serve as Left Guard General and Household Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 曄長不滿七尺，肥黑，禿眉鬚。

translations.literal: Ye's height did not reach seven chi; he was stout and dark, with bald brows and beard.
translations.idiomatic: Ye stood less than seven chi tall, stout and dark-complexioned, with scant brows and beard.

sentences.zh: 善彈琵琶，能為新聲。

translations.literal: He was skilled at playing the pipa and could compose new tunes.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at the pipa and could compose new tunes.

sentences.zh: 上欲聞之，屢諷以微旨，曄偽若不曉，終不肯為上彈。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to hear him and repeatedly hinted with subtle intent; Ye pretended not to understand and in the end would not play for the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to hear him play and repeatedly dropped hints, but Ye feigned not to understand and ultimately refused to perform for him.

sentences.zh: 上嘗宴飲歡適，謂曄曰：「我欲歌，卿可彈。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once feasted in merry ease and said to Ye: "I wish to sing—you may play."
translations.idiomatic: Once at a merry feast the emperor said to Ye, "I wish to sing—you play accompaniment."

sentences.zh: 曄乃奉旨。

translations.literal: Ye then followed the order.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Ye comply.

sentences.zh: 上歌既畢，曄亦止弦。

translations.literal: When the Emperor's song was finished, Ye also stopped the strings.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the emperor finished singing, Ye stopped playing as well.

sentences.zh: 初，魯國孔熙先博學有縱橫才志，文史星筭，無不兼善。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kong Xixian of Lu was broadly learned and had talent and will for vertical and horizontal strategy; literature, history, stars, and calculation—none he did not combine and excel in.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Kong Xixian of Lu was broadly learned and possessed talent for bold political scheming; he excelled alike in literature, history, astronomy, and mathematics.

sentences.zh: 為員外散騎侍郎，不為時所知，久不得調。

translations.literal: He was Extraordinary Gentleman Attendant at the Scattered Cavalry, not known to the age, and long could not obtain transfer.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Extraordinary Gentleman Attendant at the Scattered Cavalry but was unrecognized in his time and long went without promotion.

sentences.zh: 初熙先父默之為廣州刺史，以贓貨得罪下廷尉，大將軍彭城王義康保持之，故得免。

translations.literal: Earlier Xixian's father Mozhi was Governor of Guang Province; for bribery goods he offended and was sent down to the Minister of Justice; Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang protected him, and therefore he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian's father Mozhi had earlier served as Governor of Guang Province; convicted of bribery and sent to the Minister of Justice, he was spared through the protection of Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang.

sentences.zh: 及義康被黜，熙先密懷報效，欲要朝廷大臣，未知誰可動者，以曄意志不滿，欲引之。

translations.literal: When Yikang was demoted, Xixian secretly harbored repayment of favor; he wished to win over great ministers of the court but did not know who could be moved—because Ye's will was discontent, he wished to draw him in.
translations.idiomatic: After Yikang was demoted, Xixian secretly resolved to repay his family's debt of gratitude; he wished to win over court ministers but did not know whom he could sway. Seeing that Ye was discontent, he hoped to draw him into the plot.

sentences.zh: 而熙先素不為曄所重，無因進說。

translations.literal: Yet Xixian had never been esteemed by Ye and had no means to advance persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: But Xixian had never been esteemed by Ye and had no opportunity to approach him.

sentences.zh: 曄外甥謝綜，雅為曄所知，熙先嘗經相識，乃傾身事綜，與之結厚。

translations.literal: Ye's nephew by marriage Xie Zong was well known to Ye; Xixian had once been acquainted with him and therefore threw himself into serving Zong, forming thick bonds with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's nephew by marriage Xie Zong was well known to him; Xixian had met Zong before and therefore devoted himself to Zong and formed a close bond.

sentences.zh: 熙先藉嶺南遺財，家甚富足，始與綜諸弟共博，故為拙行，以物輸之。

translations.literal: Xixian relied on leftover wealth from Lingnan; his household was very rich. He first gambled with Zong and his younger brothers, deliberately playing clumsily and losing goods to them.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian, wealthy from his family's Lingnan fortune, began gambling with Zong and his younger brothers, deliberately playing poorly and losing goods to them.

sentences.zh: 綜等諸年少，既屢得物，遂日夕往來，情意稍款。

translations.literal: Zong and the other youths, having repeatedly gained goods, then came and went morning and evening, their feelings gradually becoming warm.
translations.idiomatic: The young men, having repeatedly won goods from him, began visiting morning and evening, and their affection gradually warmed.

sentences.zh: 綜乃引熙先與曄為數，曄又與戲，熙先故為不敵，前後輸曄物甚多。

translations.literal: Zong then introduced Xixian to gamble numbers with Ye; Ye also joined in play, and Xixian deliberately was no match, before and after losing many goods to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zong then introduced Xixian to gamble with Ye; Ye joined in as well, and Xixian deliberately lost, giving Ye a great many goods over time.

sentences.zh: 曄既利其財寶，又愛其文藝。

translations.literal: Ye both profited from his wealth and treasures and loved his literary arts.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was drawn both by his wealth and by his literary talent.

sentences.zh: 熙先素有詞辯，盡心事之，曄遂相與異常，申莫逆之好。

translations.literal: Xixian had long been skilled in rhetoric and argument; he devoted his mind to serving Ye, and Ye then associated with him beyond the ordinary, declaring friendship without estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian was eloquent and devoted himself entirely to Ye; Ye then formed an extraordinary bond with him and declared their friendship without estrangement.

sentences.zh: 始以微言動曄，曄不回，熙先乃極辭譬說。

translations.literal: At first with subtle words he moved Ye; Ye did not respond, and Xixian then used extreme rhetoric and parable to persuade.
translations.idiomatic: At first he probed Ye with subtle hints; when Ye did not respond, Xixian pressed his case with full eloquence and argument.

sentences.zh: 曄素有閨庭論議，朝野所知，故門胄雖華，而國家不與姻娶。

translations.literal: Ye had long had boudoir-and-hall disputes known to court and countryside; therefore though his gate and helmet were splendid, the state would not marry with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ye had long been known for domestic disputes discussed in court and countryside alike; though his lineage was illustrious, the throne would not marry into his family.

sentences.zh: 熙先因以此激之曰：「丈人若謂朝廷相待厚者，何故不與丈人婚，為是門戶不得邪？

translations.literal: Xixian therefore used this to incite him, saying: "If you, sir, think the court treats you generously, why does it not marry with you—is it that your gate and household are not acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Xixian used this to provoke him, saying, "If you believe the court treats you generously, why will it not marry into your house—is your lineage deemed unworthy?

sentences.zh: 人作犬豕相遇，而丈人欲為之死，不亦惑乎？」

translations.literal: Men treat one another like dogs and pigs in meeting, yet you, sir, wish to die for them—is it not deluded?"
translations.idiomatic: Men meet one another like dogs and pigs, yet you wish to die for them—is that not folly?"

sentences.zh: 曄默然不答，其意乃定。

translations.literal: Ye was silent and did not answer; his intent was then fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Ye fell silent and did not answer; his resolve was then set.

sentences.zh: 時曄與沈演之並為上所知待，每被見多同。

translations.literal: At that time Ye and Shen Yanzhi were both known and favored by the Emperor; when summoned for audience they were mostly together.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ye and Shen Yanzhi were both favored by the emperor and were usually summoned to audience together.

sentences.zh: 曄若先至，必待演之俱入；

translations.literal: If Ye arrived first, he was sure to wait for Yanzhi to enter together;
translations.idiomatic: If Ye arrived first, he always waited for Yanzhi before entering;

sentences.zh: 演之先至，嘗獨被引，曄又以此為怨。

translations.literal: if Yanzhi arrived first, he was sometimes summoned alone—Ye again took this as grievance.
translations.idiomatic: but when Yanzhi arrived first, he was sometimes admitted alone, and Ye resented this as well.

sentences.zh: 曄累經義康府佐，見待素厚。

translations.literal: Ye had repeatedly served as staff in Yikang's headquarters and had long been treated generously.
translations.idiomatic: Ye had long served on Yikang's staff and had always been treated generously by him.

sentences.zh: 及宣城之授，意好乖離。

translations.literal: When Ye received the Xuancheng appointment, their goodwill parted.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye received the Xuancheng appointment, his relationship with Yikang turned to estrangement.

sentences.zh: 綜為義康大將軍記室參軍，隨鎮豫章。

translations.literal: Zong was Recording Clerk Staff Officer to Yikang as Grand General and followed him to garrison Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong served as Recording Clerk Staff Officer on Yikang's staff as Grand General and accompanied him to his garrison at Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 綜還，申義康意於曄，求解晚隙，復敦往好。

translations.literal: When Zong returned, he conveyed Yikang's intent to Ye, seeking to resolve late rifts and restore thick former friendship.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong returned, he conveyed Yikang's wish to Ye to heal their late estrangement and restore their former closeness.

sentences.zh: 曄既有逆謀，欲探時旨，乃言於上曰：「臣歷觀前史二漢故事，諸蕃王政以訞詛幸災，便正大逆之罰。

translations.literal: Ye, having already a treasonous plot, wished to probe the times' intent and therefore said to the Emperor: "Your servant has looked through former histories and the two Han precedents: when feudal kings by policy used sorcery and curses and rejoiced in disaster, at once the great treason penalty was applied.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, already plotting rebellion, wished to test the emperor's mood and said, "Your servant has reviewed the precedents of the Former and Later Han: whenever feudal princes practiced sorcery and rejoiced at the ruler's misfortunes, they were immediately punished for great treason.

sentences.zh: 況義康姧心釁跡，彰著遐邇，而至今無恙，臣竊惑焉。

translations.literal: How much more when Yikang's treacherous heart and omen-traces are manifest far and near, yet to this day he is unharmed—your servant privately is perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Yikang's treacherous intent and misdeeds are manifest far and near, yet he remains unharmed to this day—your servant is privately perplexed.

sentences.zh: 且大梗常存，將重階亂，骨肉之際，人所難言。

translations.literal: Moreover a great obstruction constantly remains and will again step up disorder; at the juncture of flesh and bone, what men find hard to speak—
translations.idiomatic: A great threat constantly remains and may again escalate into chaos; at such a juncture among kin, others find it hard to speak plainly—

sentences.zh: 臣受恩深重，故冒犯披露。」

translations.literal: your servant has received favor deep and weighty, and therefore offends in disclosing it."
translations.idiomatic: but your servant has received such deep favor that I venture to disclose this openly."

sentences.zh: 上不納。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept his counsel.

sentences.zh: 熙先素善天文，云：「太祖必以非道晏駕，當由骨肉相殘。

translations.literal: Xixian had long been skilled at astronomy and said: "Taizu is sure to pass away by an unorthodox way; it will come from flesh-and-bone mutual slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian, skilled in astronomy, said, "Taizu is sure to die an unnatural death, brought about by mutual slaughter among kin.

sentences.zh: 江州應出天子。」

translations.literal: Jiang Province should produce the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Province is destined to produce the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 以為義康當之。

translations.literal: He believed Yikang would be the one.
translations.idiomatic: He believed Yikang was destined for this role.

sentences.zh: 綜父述亦為義康所遇，綜弟約又是義康女夫，故太祖使綜隨從南上，既為熙先所獎說，亦有酬報之心。

translations.literal: Xie Zong's father Xie Shu was also favored by Yikang; Zong's younger brother Xie Yue was moreover Yikang's son-in-law—therefore Taizu had Zong follow south; having been urged and persuaded by Xixian, he also had a heart to repay favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zong's father Xie Shu had also been favored by Yikang, and Zong's younger brother Xie Yue was Yikang's son-in-law; Taizu therefore sent Zong south with Yikang. Having been won over by Xixian, Zong too harbored a wish to repay old kindness.

sentences.zh: 廣州人周靈甫有家兵部曲，熙先以六十萬錢與之，使於廣州合兵。

translations.literal: Zhou Lingfu of Guang Province had household troops and a retinue; Xixian gave him six hundred thousand cash and had him assemble troops at Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lingfu of Guang Province had household troops; Xixian gave him six hundred thousand cash and ordered him to raise forces in Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 靈甫一去不反。

translations.literal: Lingfu went once and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Lingfu departed and never returned.

sentences.zh: 大將軍府史仲承祖，義康舊所信念，屢銜命下都，亦潛結腹心，規有異志。

translations.literal: Grand General headquarters clerk Zhong Chengzu was one Yikang had long trusted in faith; repeatedly bearing orders he went down to the capital and also secretly bound belly-and-heart men, plotting divergent intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Chengzu, a clerk in the Grand General's headquarters whom Yikang had long trusted, made repeated trips to the capital on his orders and secretly gathered trusted followers with rebellious designs.

sentences.zh: 聞熙先有誠，密相結納。

translations.literal: Hearing that Xixian was sincere, Chengzu secretly joined and accepted alliance with Xixian.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Xixian's earnest commitment, Chengzu secretly allied himself with Xixian.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹徐湛之，素為義康所愛，雖為舅甥，恩過子弟，承祖因此結事湛之，告以密計。

translations.literal: Intendant of Danyang Xu Zhanzhi had long been loved by Yikang; though uncle and nephew by marriage, favor exceeded that for sons and younger brothers—Chengzu therefore bound affairs with Zhanzhi and told him the secret plan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhanzhi, Intendant of Danyang, had long been beloved by Yikang; though uncle and nephew by marriage, Yikang favored him more than his own sons. Chengzu therefore won Zhanzhi over and disclosed the secret plot.

sentences.zh: 承祖南下，申義康意於蕭思話及曄，云：「本欲與蕭結婚，恨始意不果。

translations.literal: Chengzu went south and conveyed Yikang's intent to Xiao Sihua and Ye, saying: "Yikang originally wished to marry with Xiao and regrets that the first intent did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu went south and conveyed Yikang's wishes to Xiao Sihua and Ye, saying, "Yikang had wished to arrange a marriage with Xiao and regrets that the plan failed.

sentences.zh: 與范本情不薄，中間相失，傍人為之耳。」

translations.literal: With Fan the basic feeling was not thin; the middle estrangement between Yikang and Fan was done by bystanders, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Yikang's bond with Fan Ye was never shallow; the estrangement between them was the work of meddlers, nothing more."

sentences.zh: 有法略道人，先為義康所供養，粗被知待；

translations.literal: There was the Daoist Falüe, formerly maintained by Yikang and roughly known and treated;
translations.idiomatic: There was the Daoist Falüe, formerly supported by Yikang and moderately well regarded;

sentences.zh: 又有王國寺法靜尼亦出入義康家內，皆感激舊恩，規相拯拔，並與熙先往來。

translations.literal: there was also the nun Fajing of Wangguo Temple who also came and went within Yikang's household—all were moved by old favor and plotted mutual rescue and elevation, and all associated with Xixian.
translations.idiomatic: and the nun Fajing of Wangguo Temple also frequented Yikang's household. All were grateful for past kindness and plotted to rescue Yikang, maintaining contact with Xixian.

sentences.zh: 使法略罷道，本姓孫，改名景玄，以為臧質寧遠參軍。

translations.literal: The conspirators had Falüe leave the Way; his original surname was Sun, renamed Jingxuan, and made Staff Officer, Pacify the Far, under Zang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The conspirators had Falüe leave the priesthood; his original surname was Sun, and he was renamed Jingxuan and appointed Staff Officer under Zang Zhi, General Who Pacifies the Far.

sentences.zh: 熙先善於治病，兼能診脈。

translations.literal: Xixian was skilled at treating illness and could also examine pulses.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian was skilled at healing and could also read pulses.

sentences.zh: 法靜尼妹夫許耀，領隊在臺，宿衛殿省。

translations.literal: Fajing the nun's brother-in-law Xu Yao led a squad at the capital and guarded the palace halls overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Fajing's brother-in-law Xu Yao commanded a guard unit at the capital and performed overnight duty in the palace.

sentences.zh: 嘗有病，因法靜尼就熙先乞治，為合湯一劑，耀疾即損。

translations.literal: Yao once had illness; through Fajing the nun he begged Xixian for treatment; Xixian compounded one dose of decoction and Yao's illness at once diminished.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao once fell ill, he asked Fajing to seek treatment from Xixian; Xixian prepared a dose of medicine and Yao's illness quickly improved.

sentences.zh: 耀自往酬謝，因成周旋。

translations.literal: Yao himself went to repay thanks and thereby formed social exchange with Xixian.
translations.idiomatic: Yao went in person to thank Xixian and thus entered into association with Xixian.

sentences.zh: 熙先以耀膽幹可施，深相待結，因告逆謀，耀許為內應。

translations.literal: Xixian, because Yao's courage and backbone could be applied, deeply treated and bound him, and therefore told the treasonous plot; Yao promised to be inner response.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian, seeing that Yao's courage could be put to use, drew him into a close bond and disclosed the plot; Yao agreed to serve as an inside collaborator.

sentences.zh: 豫章胡遵世，藩之子也，與法略甚款，亦密相酬和。

translations.literal: Hu Zunshi of Yuzhang, son of Fan, was on very warm terms with Falüe and also secretly responded in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zunshi of Yuzhang, son of Hu Fan, was on intimate terms with Falüe and also secretly joined the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 法靜尼南上，熙先遣婢採藻隨之，付以箋書，陳說圖讖。

translations.literal: Fajing the nun went south; Xixian sent the maid Caizao to follow her, entrusting her with letters and setting forth charts and prophecies.
translations.idiomatic: When Fajing went south, Xixian sent the maid Caizao with her, bearing letters that set forth charts and prophecies.

sentences.zh: 法靜還，義康餉熙先銅匕、銅鑷、袍段、棊奩等物。

translations.literal: When Fajing returned, Yikang sent Xixian gifts of bronze spoon, bronze tweezers, robe lengths, chess casket, and other objects.
translations.idiomatic: When Fajing returned, Yikang sent Xixian gifts of a bronze spoon, bronze tweezers, lengths of robe cloth, a chess case, and other items.

sentences.zh: 熙先慮事泄，鴆採藻殺之。

translations.literal: Xixian feared the matter would leak and poisoned Caizao to kill her.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the plot would leak, Xixian poisoned Caizao to death.

sentences.zh: 湛之又謂曄等：「臧質見與異常，歲內當還，已報質，悉攜門生義故，其亦當解人此旨，故應得健兒數百。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi again said to Ye and others: "Zang Zhi's treatment of me is beyond the ordinary; within the year he should return—I have already reported to Zhi to bring all his students and old associates; he too should understand men's intent here, and therefore ought to obtain several hundred stalwart youths.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi told Ye and the others, "Zang Zhi treats me with exceptional favor and should return within the year. I have already informed Zhi to bring all his students and old associates; he should understand our purpose and can supply several hundred stalwart fighters.

sentences.zh: 質與蕭思話款密，當仗要之，二人並受大將軍眷遇，必無異同。

translations.literal: Zhi and Xiao Sihua are on warm and close terms—we should rely on and require them; both received the Grand General's fond favor and surely will not differ.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Xiao Sihua are on intimate terms and must be enlisted; both received the Grand General's favor and will surely not waver.

sentences.zh: 思話三州義故眾力，亦不減質。

translations.literal: Sihua's three provinces of old associates and multitude of strength are also not less than Zhi's.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua's followers across three provinces are no fewer in strength than Zhi's.

sentences.zh: 郡中文武，及合諸處偵邏，亦當不減千人。

translations.literal: Civil and military within the commandery, together with scouts and patrols from all places combined, should also be not less than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military officials of the commandery, together with scouts and patrols from various posts, should also amount to no fewer than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 不憂兵力不足，但當勿失機耳。」

translations.literal: We need not worry that military strength is insufficient—we need only not miss the opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: We need not worry about insufficient force—only about missing the opportunity."

sentences.zh: 乃略相署置，湛之為撫軍將軍、揚州刺史；

translations.literal: They then roughly assigned posts among themselves: Zhanzhi as General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Yang Province;
translations.idiomatic: They then roughly assigned future posts: Zhanzhi as General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Yang Province;

sentences.zh: 曄中軍將軍、南徐州刺史；

translations.literal: Ye as General of the Center Army and Governor of Southern Xu Province;
translations.idiomatic: Ye as General of the Center Army and Governor of Southern Xu Province;

sentences.zh: 熙先左衛將軍，其餘皆有選擬。

translations.literal: Xixian as General of the Left Guard—the rest all had selections drafted.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian as General of the Left Guard—the rest likewise had posts chosen for them.

sentences.zh: 凡素所不善及不附義康者，又有別簿，竝入死目。

translations.literal: All whom they had long disliked and who did not attach to Yikang had a separate register—all entered the death list.
translations.idiomatic: Those they had long disliked and all who did not side with Yikang were entered on a separate register—all marked for death.

sentences.zh: 熙先使弟休先先為檄文曰：

translations.literal: Xixian had his younger brother Kong Xiuxian first draft a proclamation, which said:
translations.idiomatic: Xixian had his younger brother Kong Xiuxian draft a proclamation that read:

sentences.zh: 夫休否相乘，道無恆泰，狂狡肆逆，明哲是殛。

translations.literal: Prosperity and adversity multiply upon one another; the Way has no constant peace—when the mad and cunning wildly rebel, the clear-sighted are the ones who strike them down.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and misfortune follow upon one another; the Way knows no lasting peace. When the mad and cunning rise in rebellion, the wise are the ones who strike them down.

sentences.zh: 故小白有一匡之勳，重耳有翼戴之德。

translations.literal: Therefore Duke Huan of Qi had the merit of one rectification, and Duke Wen of Jin had the virtue of winging and bearing up the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Duke Huan of Qi earned the merit of restoring order to the realm, and Duke Wen of Jin earned the virtue of supporting the throne.

sentences.zh: 自景平肇始，皇室多故，大行皇帝天誕英姿，聰明睿哲，拔自藩國，嗣位統天，憂勞萬機，垂心庶務，是以邦內安逸，四海同風。

translations.literal: From the beginning of the Jingping era the imperial house had many troubles; the late emperor was heaven-born in heroic bearing, bright and wise, drawn up from a feudal state to succeed the throne and unite under Heaven, toiling over the myriad affairs and lowering his heart to the multitude of duties—therefore within the realm there was ease, and the four seas shared one wind.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning of the Jingping era the imperial house suffered many troubles. The late emperor was heaven-born in heroic bearing, bright and wise; raised from a feudal domain to succeed the throne and rule all under Heaven, he toiled over myriad affairs and devoted himself to governance—so that the realm was at ease and the four seas shared one purpose.

sentences.zh: 而比年以來，姧豎亂政，刑罰乖淫，陰陽違舛，致使釁起蕭牆，危禍萃集。

translations.literal: Yet in recent years treacherous minions have disordered government, punishments have been perverse and excessive, yin and yang have violated and gone awry—causing trouble to rise within the palace walls and peril and disaster to gather together.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in recent years treacherous minions have thrown government into chaos, punishments have run perverse and excessive, and yin and yang have fallen out of harmony—so that trouble has risen within the palace and peril has gathered on every side.

sentences.zh: 賊臣趙伯符積怨含毒，遂縱姧凶，肆兵犯蹕，禍流儲宰，崇樹非類，傾墜皇基。

translations.literal: The traitor minister Zhao Bofu, storing resentment and holding poison, then unleashed treachery and villainy, wantonly deploying troops to violate the imperial progress; disaster flowed to the heir and chief minister, he exalted and planted improper kinds, and toppled and crashed the imperial foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The traitor Zhao Bofu, nursing resentment and malice, unleashed treachery and villainy, wantonly raised troops against the imperial procession, brought disaster upon the heir and chief ministers, exalted unworthy men, and threatened to overturn the imperial foundation.

sentences.zh: 罪百浞、豷，過十玄、莽，開闢以來，未聞斯比。

translations.literal: His crimes exceed a hundredfold those of Zhou and Yan, his excesses surpass tenfold those of Xuan and Mang—since the opening of the age, none such as this has been heard.
translations.idiomatic: His crimes exceed those of Zhou and Yan a hundredfold, his excesses surpass those of Wang Mang tenfold—since the beginning of history, nothing like this has been heard.

sentences.zh: 率土叩心，華夷泣血，咸懷亡身之誠，同思糜軀之報。

translations.literal: All within the lands beat their breasts, Chinese and barbarians wept blood—all harbored sincerity to lose their bodies, together thinking to grind their persons in repayment.
translations.idiomatic: All within the realm beat their breasts in grief; Chinese and barbarians wept blood—all harbored the will to give their lives, together longing to sacrifice themselves in repayment.

sentences.zh: 湛之、曄與行中領軍蕭思話、行護軍將軍臧質、行左衛將軍孔熙先、建威將軍孔休先，忠貫白日，誠著幽顯，義痛其心，事傷其目，投命奮戈，萬殞莫顧，即日斬伯符首，及其黨與。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi, Ye, Acting General of the Center Army Xiao Sihua, Acting General Who Protects the Army Zang Zhi, Acting General of the Left Guard Kong Xixian, and General Who Establishes Might Kong Xiuxian, Xixian's younger brother—loyalty pierced the white sun, sincerity showed in hidden and manifest; righteousness pained their hearts, affairs wounded their eyes; they cast their lives and brandished weapons, ten thousand deaths unheeded, and on that day cut off Bofu's head and his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi, Ye, Acting General of the Center Army Xiao Sihua, Acting General Who Protects the Army Zang Zhi, Acting General of the Left Guard Kong Xixian, and General Who Establishes Might Kong Xiuxian, Xixian's younger brother—loyalty shining like the sun, sincerity manifest in hidden and open realms—were pained in heart and wounded in spirit; they risked their lives and brandished weapons, heedless of ten thousand deaths, and on that day cut off Bofu's head and his faction.

sentences.zh: 雖豺狼即戮，王道惟新，而普天無主，群萌莫繼。

translations.literal: Though the wolf was at once punished, the kingly Way was only renewed—yet all under Heaven had no lord, and the multitude of sprouts had none to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Though the wolf was at once punished and the kingly Way renewed, all under Heaven lacked a ruler, and the people had none to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 彭城王體自高祖，聖明在躬，德格天地，勳溢區宇，世路威夷，勿用南服，龍潛鳳棲，於茲六稔，蒼生饑德，億兆渴化，豈唯東征有《鴟鴞》之歌，陝西有勿翦之思哉！

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng in body descends from Gaozu; sagely brightness is in his person, virtue reaches heaven and earth, merit overflows the realm; the age's road was awe-inspiring and level, yet he was not used in southern service—dragon hidden, phoenix perched, for six harvest-years here; the black-haired people hunger for virtue, the hundred millions thirst for transformation—is it only that the eastern campaign had the 'Owl' song, and west of the passes there was the thought of do not cut down!
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng springs from Gaozu's line; sagely brilliance is in his person, his virtue reaches heaven and earth, his merit fills the realm. Though the age's road was level and awe-inspiring, he was not employed in southern service—like a dragon hidden and a phoenix perched these six years. The people hunger for his virtue; the millions thirst for his rule—is it only in the east that they sing the 'Owl,' and west of the passes that they cry, do not cut him down?

sentences.zh: 靈祗告徵祥之應，讖記表帝者之符，上答天心，下愜民望，正位辰極，非王而誰？

translations.literal: Spirits and gods proclaimed responses of auspicious omens; charts and records displayed the talismans of an emperor—above answering heaven's heart, below satisfying the people's hopes—to set the throne at the celestial pole—if not the prince, who?
translations.idiomatic: Spirits and gods proclaimed auspicious omens; prophecies displayed the marks of an emperor—answering heaven's will above and the people's hopes below—to take the throne at the celestial pole—if not the prince, who else?

sentences.zh: 今遣行護軍將軍臧質等，齎皇帝璽綬，星馳奉迎。

translations.literal: Now we dispatch Acting General Who Protects the Army Zang Zhi and others, bearing the imperial seal and cord, to welcome him at star speed.
translations.idiomatic: We now dispatch Acting General Who Protects the Army Zang Zhi and others, bearing the imperial seal and cord, to welcome him with all speed.

sentences.zh: 百官備禮，駱驛繼進，並命群帥，鎮戍有常。

translations.literal: The hundred officials prepare ritual; relay horses advance in succession; all commanders of hosts are ordered—garrisons and guards hold their stations.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials prepare ceremonial observances; relay horses advance in succession; all commanders are ordered to hold their garrisons as usual.

sentences.zh: 若干撓義徒，有犯無貸。

translations.literal: Should any obstruct the righteous cause, offense will not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever obstructs the righteous cause shall not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 昔年使反，湛之奉賜手敕，逆誡禍亂，預睹斯萌，令宣示朝賢，共拯危溺，無斷謀事，失於後機，遂使聖躬濫酷，大變奄集，哀恨崩裂，撫心摧哽，不知何地，可以厝身。

translations.literal: In former years when the envoy returned, Zhanzhi received the bestowed hand edict, admonishing against disaster and disorder, foreseeing this sprout, and was ordered to proclaim to court worthies to together rescue peril and drowning—but without decisive plotting he missed the later opportunity, and thus the sage person suffered excessive cruelty, great change suddenly gathered; grief and hatred split apart, stroking the heart and choking the throat—he knew not what place could set his body.
translations.idiomatic: In former years when the envoy returned, Zhanzhi received the emperor's handwritten edict warning against disaster and disorder and foreseeing this danger, ordering him to proclaim to court worthies to rescue the realm together—but lacking resolve in plotting he missed the crucial moment, so that the sacred person suffered cruel death and great calamity suddenly fell. Grief and hatred split his heart; stroking his breast he choked with anguish, not knowing where he might place himself.

sentences.zh: 輒督厲尪頓，死而後已。

translations.literal: He thereupon urged and spurred the weak and stumbling, until death then stopping.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore urged on the weak and faltering, resolved not to stop until death.

sentences.zh: 熙先以既為大事，宜須義康意旨，曄乃作義康與湛之書，宣示同黨曰：

translations.literal: Xixian, because the matter was already great, held that Yikang's intent was necessary; Ye therefore composed a letter from Yikang to Zhanzhi and displayed it to the fellow partisans, which said:
translations.idiomatic: Xixian held that so great an undertaking required Yikang's endorsement; Ye therefore forged a letter from Yikang to Zhanzhi and showed it to the conspirators, which read:

sentences.zh: 吾凡人短才，生長富貴，任情用己，有過不聞，與物無恆，喜怒違實，致使小人多怨，士類不歸。

translations.literal: I am a common man of short talent, grown up in wealth and honor, indulging feeling and using self; when I had faults I did not hear of them; toward things I had no constancy; joy and anger departed from reality—causing petty men many grievances and the gentry class not to return.
translations.idiomatic: I am a common man of limited talent, raised in wealth and honor, indulging my whims; when I erred I heard no correction; I was inconstant toward others; my joy and anger bore no relation to reality—so that petty men bore many grudges against me and the gentry would not rally to me.

sentences.zh: 禍敗已成，猶不覺悟，退加尋省，方知自招，刻肌刻骨，何所復補。

translations.literal: Disaster and defeat were already formed, yet I still did not awaken; withdrawing I added searching reflection and then knew I had summoned it myself—carved into flesh and bone, what could again be mended?
translations.idiomatic: Disaster and defeat were already upon me, yet I still did not awaken; only in retreat did I reflect and know I had brought it on myself—etched into flesh and bone, what could now be repaired?

sentences.zh: 然至於盡心奉上，誠貫幽顯，拳拳謹慎，惟恐不及，乃可恃寵驕盈，實不敢故為欺罔也。

translations.literal: Yet as to devoting my mind to serving above, sincerity piercing hidden and manifest, earnest and cautious, fearing only that I could not reach sufficiency—how could I rely on favor and be proud and full? I truly did not dare deliberately to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in devoting my heart to serving the throne, my sincerity pierced hidden and manifest realms; earnest and cautious, I feared only falling short—how could I rely on favor and grow arrogant? I truly did not dare deliberately to deceive.

sentences.zh: 豈苞藏逆心，以招灰滅，所以推誠自信，不復防護異同，率意信心，不顧萬物議論，遂致讒巧潛構，眾惡歸集。

translations.literal: How could I harbor treasonous heart to summon ashes and extinction?
