Therefore I pushed sincerity and trusted myself, no longer guarding against difference and sameness, following intent and trusting heart, not heeding the myriad things' discussion—thus causing slanderous craft to construct in secret and the multitude of evils to gather upon me.
translations.idiomatic: How could I harbor treasonous intent and invite destruction? Therefore I gave my sincerity and trusted myself, no longer guarding against dissent, following my inclinations and trusting my heart, heedless of what others said—thus allowing slanderers to plot in secret and every evil to gather against me.

sentences.zh: 甲姧險好利，負吾事深；

translations.literal: A is treacherous, dangerous, and greedy for profit, and has deeply failed my affairs;
translations.idiomatic: A is treacherous, dangerous, and greedy, and has deeply wronged me;

sentences.zh: 乙凶愚不齒，扇長無賴；

translations.literal: B is fierce, stupid, and not of our rank, fanning and growing the worthless;
translations.idiomatic: B is fierce, stupid, and base, fanning the worthless;

sentences.zh: 丙、丁趨走小子，唯知諂進，伺求長短，共造虛說，致令禍陷骨肉，誅戮無辜。

translations.literal: C and D are running attendants and youths who know only flattery and advance, watching to seek strengths and weaknesses, together fabricating empty talk, causing disaster to trap flesh and bone and executions of the guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: C and D are servile youths who know only flattery, watching for faults, together fabricating lies, bringing disaster upon kin and executing the innocent.

sentences.zh: 凡在過釁，竟有何徴，而刑罰所加，同之元惡，傷和枉理，感徹天地。

translations.literal: All who were in passing fault—what signs did they finally have? Yet punishments applied treated them the same as the chief evil, harming harmony and bending principle, moving and penetrating heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: All who had minor faults—what proof was there? Yet the punishments applied treated them as chief villains, harming harmony and bending justice, moving heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 吾雖幽逼日苦，命在漏刻，義慨之士，時有音信。

translations.literal: Though I am confined and pressed daily in bitterness, my life in the dripping clepsydra, men of righteous indignation from time to time have messages.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am confined daily in bitterness and my life hangs by a thread, men of righteous indignation send word from time to time.

sentences.zh: 每知天文人事，及外間物情，土崩瓦解，必在朝夕。

translations.literal: Each time I know astronomy and human affairs, and the feelings of things outside, earth collapses and tiles crumble—it must be within morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I learn of heaven's signs and human affairs, and of sentiment beyond these walls, the realm's collapse must come within days.

sentences.zh: 是為釁起群賢，濫延國家，夙夜憤踴，心復交戰。

translations.literal: This is because trouble rises among the worthies and overflows to the state; morning and evening I am indignant and leaping, my heart again battling within.
translations.idiomatic: Because trouble rises among the worthy and overflows upon the state, morning and evening I burn with indignation, my heart battling within.

sentences.zh: 朝之君子及士庶白黑懷義秉理者，寧可不識時運之會，而坐待橫流邪？

translations.literal: The court's gentlemen and gentry and commoners, black and white, who harbor righteousness and hold to principle—can they fail to know the juncture of the times' fortune, and sit waiting for the crossflow?
translations.idiomatic: Can the gentlemen of court, the gentry and commoners of every rank who harbor righteousness and hold to principle, fail to recognize the turning of the times and sit waiting for the flood to sweep them away?

sentences.zh: 除君側之惡，非唯一代，況此等狂亂罪辠骫，終古所無，加之翦戮，易於摧朽邪！

translations.literal: Removing evils beside the ruler is not unique to one generation; moreover such mad, chaotic crimes of wickedness have never existed from antiquity—to add cutting down and slaughter would be easier than crushing rotten wood!
translations.idiomatic: Removing evils from the ruler's side is nothing new in history; yet crimes as mad and wicked as these have never been seen before. To cut them down and slaughter them would be easier than snapping rotten timber!

sentences.zh: 可以吾意宣示眾賢，若能同心奮發，族裂逆黨，豈非功均創業，重造宋室乎！

translations.literal: You may proclaim my intent to the assembled worthies; if you can join hearts and rouse yourselves, exterminate the rebel faction by clan—would that not be merit equal to founding the realm, remaking the House of Song!
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim my intent to the assembled worthies: if you can join hearts and rouse yourselves to exterminate the rebel faction root and branch, would that not be merit equal to founding the dynasty and remaking the House of Song?

sentences.zh: 但兵凶戰危，或致侵濫，若有一豪犯順，誅及九族。

translations.literal: But arms are baleful and battle perilous, and may lead to excess; if a single bold man violates obedience, execution will reach nine degrees of kin.
translations.idiomatic: But arms are baleful and battle perilous, and may lead to excess; if a single man of bold spirit defies authority, punishment will reach nine degrees of kin.

sentences.zh: 處分之要，委之群賢，皆當謹奉朝廷，動止聞啟。

translations.literal: The essentials of disposition, entrust to the assembled worthies; all must reverently obey the court, reporting movements and stops.
translations.idiomatic: The essentials of how affairs are to be handled I entrust to the assembled worthies; all must reverently obey the court and report every move.

sentences.zh: 往日嫌怨，一時豁然，然後吾當謝罪北闕，就戮有司。

translations.literal: Past grievances and resentments, all at once cleared away; then I shall confess guilt at the northern gate and submit to execution by the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Let past grievances and resentments be cleared away at once; then I shall confess my guilt at the northern gate and submit to execution by the officials.

sentences.zh: 苟安社稷，瞑目無恨。

translations.literal: If the altars of state are secured, I close my eyes without regret.
translations.idiomatic: If the altars of state are secured, I can close my eyes without regret.

sentences.zh: 勉之，勉之！

translations.literal: Press on! Press on!
translations.idiomatic: Press on! Press on!

sentences.zh: 二十二年九月，征北將軍衡陽王義季、右將軍南平王鑠出鎮，上於武帳岡祖道，曄等期以其日為亂，而差互不得發。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-second year, Northern Expedition General Prince of Hengyang Yiji and Right General Prince of Nanping Shuo departed to take up their garrison commands; the Emperor held a farewell ceremony at Wuzhang Mound; Ye and the others had planned to rebel on that day, but mishaps prevented them from acting.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-second year, the Northern Expedition General, Prince of Hengyang Yiji, and the Right General, Prince of Nanping Shuo, departed to take up their provincial commands. The Emperor held a farewell ceremony for them at Wuzhang Mound. Ye and his co-conspirators had planned to launch their rebellion on that day, but mishaps prevented them from acting.

sentences.zh: 於十一月，徐湛之上表曰：「臣與范曄，本無素舊，中忝門下，與之鄰省，屢來見就，故漸成周旋。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Xu Zhanzhi submitted a memorial stating: "Your servant and Fan Ye had no former acquaintance; midway I was honored in the Gate Chamber staff, adjacent province to his—he repeatedly came to visit me, and thus we gradually became familiar.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Xu Zhanzhi submitted a memorial stating: "Your servant and Fan Ye had no former acquaintance. I was later honored with a post on the Gate Chamber staff, in an office adjacent to his; he repeatedly came to visit me, and thus we gradually became familiar.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，意態轉見，傾動險忌，富貴情深，自謂任遇未高，遂生怨望。

translations.literal: In recent years his attitude grew increasingly visible—restless, swaying toward danger and jealousy, his attachment to wealth and rank deep; deeming his appointments insufficiently high, he nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years his attitude grew increasingly apparent—restless, prone to danger and jealousy, deeply attached to wealth and rank. Deeming his appointments insufficiently lofty, he nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 非唯攻伐朝士，譏謗聖時，乃上議朝廷，下及藩輔，驅扇同異，恣口肆心，如此之事，已具上簡。

translations.literal: Not only attacking court officials and slandering the sacred age—he spoke ill of the court above and the princely supporters below, inciting factions, giving free rein to mouth and heart; such matters are fully set out in my earlier memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He not only attacked court officials and slandered the sacred age; he spoke ill of the court above and the princely supporters below, inciting factions and giving free rein to mouth and heart. Such matters are fully set out in my earlier memorial.

sentences.zh: 近員外散騎侍郎孔熙先忽令大將軍府吏仲承祖騰曄及謝綜等意，欲收合不逞，規有所建。

translations.literal: Recently the Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Kong Xixian suddenly sent the Grand General's office clerk Zhong Chengzu to convey Ye's and Xie Zong's intentions—they wished to gather the unruly and plot some undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Kong Xixian suddenly sent the Grand General's office clerk Zhong Chengzu to convey the intentions of Ye and Xie Zong—they wished to gather the unruly and plot some undertaking.

sentences.zh: 以臣昔蒙義康接盼，又去歲群小為臣妄生風塵，謂必嫌懼，深見勸誘。

translations.literal: Because your servant was once favored by Yikang in the past, and because petty men last year stirred up trouble for me in vain, they assumed I must harbor fear and resentment, and pressed me deeply with persuasion and enticement.
translations.idiomatic: Because your servant had once been favored by Yikang, and because petty men last year stirred up trouble for me in vain, they assumed I must harbor fear and resentment, and pressed me deeply with persuasion and enticement.

sentences.zh: 兼云人情樂亂，機不可失，讖緯天文，竝有徵驗。

translations.literal: They also said that human hearts delighted in chaos, the opportunity must not be missed, and omen texts and astronomical signs both showed corroborating evidence.
translations.idiomatic: They also said that people delighted in chaos, that the opportunity must not be missed, and that omen texts and astronomical signs all showed corroborating evidence.

sentences.zh: 曄尋自來，復具陳此，並說臣論議轉惡，全身為難。

translations.literal: Ye soon came in person and again fully described this, also saying my discussions had turned worse and that preserving myself would be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Ye soon came in person and again fully described this, also saying that my discussions had turned worse and that preserving myself would be difficult.

sentences.zh: 即以啟聞，被敕使相酬引，究其情狀。

translations.literal: I immediately reported this; I received an edict to engage him in mutual probing and investigate the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: I immediately reported this and received an edict to engage him in mutual probing and investigate the circumstances.

sentences.zh: 於是悉出檄書、選事、及同惡人名、手墨翰跡，謹封上呈，凶悖之甚，古今罕比。

translations.literal: Thereupon I produced all proclamations, recruitment orders, and the names of co-conspirators, with handwriting and brush traces, sealed and submitted—treasonous extremity rare in past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon I produced all proclamations, recruitment orders, the names of co-conspirators, and their handwriting and brush traces, sealed and submitted—treason of an extremity rare in past and present.

sentences.zh: 由臣闇於交士，聞此逆謀，臨啟震惶，荒情無措。」

translations.literal: Because your servant was blind in choosing companions, hearing this treasonous plot, when I opened the report I was shaken with terror, my mind in chaos unable to act."
translations.idiomatic: Because your servant was blind in choosing companions, on hearing this treasonous plot and opening the report I was shaken with terror, my mind in chaos and unable to act."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「湛之表如此，良可駭惋。

translations.literal: The edict stated: "Zhanzhi's memorial is as this—truly shocking and lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: The edict stated: "Zhanzhi's memorial is as this—truly shocking and lamentable.

sentences.zh: 曄素無行檢，少負瑕釁，但以才藝可施，故收其所長，頻加榮爵，遂參清顯。

translations.literal: Ye has always lacked moral conduct; in youth he bore blemishes and guilt, yet because his talent and skill could be employed, his strengths were taken in, honors and titles repeatedly added, and he reached clear and eminent rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ye has always lacked moral conduct and in youth bore blemishes and guilt; yet because his talent and skill could be employed, his strengths were taken in, honors and titles repeatedly added, until he reached clear and eminent rank.

sentences.zh: 而險利之性，有過溪壑，不識恩遇，猶懷怨憤。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was grasping and dangerous as a ravine—he did not recognize imperial grace, still harbored resentment and rage.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature was grasping and dangerous as a ravine; he did not recognize the grace shown him and still harbored resentment and rage.

sentences.zh: 每存容養，冀能悛革，不謂同惡相濟，狂悖至此。

translations.literal: Each time we indulged and nurtured him, hoping he might repent and reform; who could have thought he would aid evil companions and become madly rebellious to this degree?
translations.idiomatic: Each time we indulged and nurtured him, hoping he might repent and reform; who could have thought he would aid evil companions and become madly rebellious to this degree?

sentences.zh: 便可收掩，依法窮詰。」

translations.literal: Now arrest and detain him; investigate to the full according to law."
translations.idiomatic: Arrest and detain him now, and investigate to the full according to law."

sentences.zh: 其夜，先呼曄及朝臣集華林東閣，止於客省。

translations.literal: That night, the authorities first summoned Ye and court ministers to assemble at the eastern pavilion of Hualin, confining them in the guest quarters.
translations.idiomatic: That night the authorities first summoned Ye and the court ministers to assemble at the eastern pavilion of Hualin, confining them in the guest quarters.

sentences.zh: 先已於外收綜及熙先兄弟，竝皆款服。

translations.literal: The authorities had already arrested Zong and Xixian's brothers outside—all fully confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities had already arrested Xie Zong and Kong Xixian's brothers outside—all had fully confessed.

sentences.zh: 于時上在延賢堂，遣使問曄曰：「以卿觕有文翰，故相任擢，名爵期懷，於例非少。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was in the Yancian Hall and sent a messenger to question Ye: "Because you roughly have literary talent, you were entrusted and promoted; titles and ranks as you hoped—not few by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor was in the Yancian Hall and sent a messenger to question Ye: "Because you have some literary talent, you were entrusted and promoted; the titles and ranks you hoped for were not few by precedent.

sentences.zh: 亦知卿意難厭滿，正是無理怨望，驅扇朋黨而已，云何乃有異謀？」

translations.literal: We also know your heart is hard to satisfy—but this is merely unreasonable resentment, inciting partisan cliques—why then would you have designs of rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: We also know your heart is hard to satisfy—but this is merely unreasonable resentment and inciting partisan cliques. Why then would you harbor designs of rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 曄倉卒怖懼，不即首款。

translations.literal: Ye, in sudden terror, did not immediately confess.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, in sudden terror, did not immediately confess.

sentences.zh: 上重遣問曰：「卿與謝綜、徐湛之、孔熙先謀逆，竝已答款，猶尚未死，徵據見存，何不依實。」

translations.literal: The Emperor sent again to ask: "You plotted rebellion with Xie Zong, Xu Zhanzhi, and Kong Xixian—all have answered and confessed, are not yet dead, and documentary evidence still exists—why not speak according to fact?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent again to ask: "You plotted rebellion with Xie Zong, Xu Zhanzhi, and Kong Xixian—all have confessed, are not yet dead, and documentary evidence still exists. Why not speak according to the facts?"

sentences.zh: 曄對曰：「今宗室磐石，蕃嶽張跱，設使竊發僥倖，方鎮便來討伐，幾何而不誅夷？

translations.literal: Ye replied: "Now the imperial clans are bedrock, the frontier princes stand deployed—suppose one rashly acted on a gamble, the territorial commanders would at once come to suppress and punish—how long before annihilation?
translations.idiomatic: Ye replied: "Now the imperial clans are bedrock and the frontier princes stand deployed. Suppose one rashly acted on a gamble—the territorial commanders would at once come to suppress and punish. How long before annihilation?

sentences.zh: 且臣位任過重，一階兩級，自然必至，如何以滅族易此。

translations.literal: Moreover my position and appointment are already weighty—one or two ranks more would naturally come—why exchange this for extinction of the clan?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my position and appointment are already weighty—one or two ranks more would naturally come. Why exchange this for the extinction of my clan?

sentences.zh: 古人云：『左手據天下之圖，右手刎其喉，愚夫不為。』

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'The left hand holds the map of all under Heaven, the right hand cuts one's own throat—even a fool would not do it.'
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: 'The left hand holds the map of all under Heaven while the right hand cuts one's own throat—even a fool would not do it.'

sentences.zh: 臣雖泥下，朝廷許其觕有所及，以理而察，臣不容有此。」

translations.literal: Though I am mud below, the court allowed my rough abilities some scope—examining by reason, I cannot have this."
translations.idiomatic: Though I am lowly as mud, the court allowed my rough abilities some scope. Examining the matter by reason, I cannot have done this."

sentences.zh: 上復遣問曰：「熙先近在華林門外，寧欲面辨之乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor sent again to ask: "Xixian is presently just outside the Hualin gate—would you care to confront him face to face?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent again to ask: "Xixian is presently just outside the Hualin gate—would you care to confront him face to face?"

sentences.zh: 曄辭窮，乃曰：「熙先苟誣引臣，臣當如何！」

translations.literal: Ye, arguments exhausted, said: "If Xixian falsely implicates me, what am I to do!"
translations.idiomatic: Ye, his arguments exhausted, said: "If Xixian falsely implicates me, what am I to do!"

sentences.zh: 熙先聞曄不服，笑謂殿中將軍沈邵之曰：「凡諸處分，符檄書疏，皆范曄所造及治定。

translations.literal: Xixian, hearing Ye would not admit guilt, laughed and said to the Palace Guard general Shen Shaozhi: "All orders of disposition, seals, documents, and letters were drafted and finalized by Fan Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian, hearing that Ye would not admit guilt, laughed and said to the Palace Guard general Shen Shaozhi: "All orders of disposition, seals, documents, and letters were drafted and finalized by Fan Ye.

sentences.zh: 云何於今方作如此抵蹋邪！」

translations.literal: Why now make such evasive repudiation!"
translations.idiomatic: Why make such evasive repudiation only now!"

sentences.zh: 上示以墨跡，曄乃具陳本末，曰：「久欲上聞，逆謀未著。

translations.literal: The Emperor showed him the handwriting; Ye then fully narrated the sequence, saying: "Long I wished to report upward, but the treason had not yet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor showed him the handwriting; Ye then fully narrated the sequence, saying: "Long I wished to report upward, but the treason had not yet appeared.

sentences.zh: 又冀其事消弭，故推遷至今。

translations.literal: I also hoped the matter might dissolve, so I deferred until now.
translations.idiomatic: I also hoped the matter might dissolve, and so I deferred until now.

sentences.zh: 負國罪重，分甘誅戮。」

translations.literal: Guilt against the state is heavy; I willingly accept execution."
translations.idiomatic: My guilt against the state is heavy; I willingly accept execution."

sentences.zh: 其夜，上使尚書僕射何尚之視之，問曰：「卿事何得至此？」

translations.literal: That night the Emperor had the Vice Director of the Masters of Writing He Shangzhi visit and question him: "How did your affair come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: That night the Emperor had the Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, He Shangzhi, visit and question him: "How did your affair come to this?"

sentences.zh: 曄曰：「君謂是何？」

translations.literal: Ye said: "What does my lord think it is?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: "What does my lord think it is?"

sentences.zh: 尚之曰：「卿自應解。」

translations.literal: He Shangzhi said: "You ought to know yourself."
translations.idiomatic: He Shangzhi said: "You ought to know yourself."

sentences.zh: 曄曰：「外人傳庾尚書見憎，計與之無惡。

translations.literal: Ye said: "Outsiders say the Master of Writing Yu bears ill will toward me—I reckon there is no enmity between us.
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: "Outsiders say the Master of Writing Yu bears ill will toward me—I reckon there is no enmity between us.

sentences.zh: 謀遂之事，聞孔熙先說此，輕其小兒，不以經意。

translations.literal: When the plot was being discussed, I heard Kong Xixian speak of this—I thought lightly of the boy and did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was being discussed, I heard Kong Xixian speak of this. I thought lightly of the boy and did not take it to heart.

sentences.zh: 今忽受責，方覺為罪。

translations.literal: Now suddenly bearing blame, I finally realize it is a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Now suddenly bearing blame, I finally realize it is a crime.

sentences.zh: 君方以道佐世，使天下無冤。

translations.literal: My lord now assists the age with the Way, making the realm without injustice.
translations.idiomatic: My lord now assists the age with the Way, making the realm free of injustice.

sentences.zh: 弟就死之後，猶望君照此心也。」

translations.literal: After your younger brother goes to his death, I still hope my lord will illumine this heart."
translations.idiomatic: After your younger brother goes to his death, I still hope my lord will recognize this heart."

sentences.zh: 明日，仗士送曄付廷尉，入獄，問徐丹陽所在，然後知為湛之所發。

translations.literal: The next day, armed guards escorted Ye to the Court of Justice; entering prison, he asked where Xu Zhanzhi, the Danyang Intendant, was—only then learning it was Zhanzhi who had denounced him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day armed guards escorted Ye to the Court of Justice. Entering prison, he asked where Xu Zhanzhi, the Danyang Intendant, was—only then learning it was Zhanzhi who had denounced him.

sentences.zh: 熙先望風吐款，辭氣不橈，上奇其才，遣人慰勞之曰：「以卿之才，而滯於集書省，理應有異志。

translations.literal: Xixian, sensing the wind, confessed fully; his words and bearing did not bend—the Emperor marveled at his talent and sent someone to comfort him: "With your talents, yet stagnant in the Secretariat—naturally you would harbor different ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian, sensing which way the wind blew, confessed fully; his words and bearing did not bend. The Emperor marveled at his talent and sent someone to comfort him: "With your talents, yet stagnant in the Secretariat—naturally you would harbor different ambitions.

sentences.zh: 此乃我負卿也。」

translations.literal: This is I who failed you."
translations.idiomatic: This is I who failed you."

sentences.zh: 又詰責前吏部尚書何尚之曰：「使孔熙先年將三十作散騎郎，那不作賊！」

translations.literal: He also sternly rebuked the former Minister of Personnel He Shangzhi: "Had you made Kong Xixian an Attendant Cavalier at nearly thirty, he would not have become a rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: He also sternly rebuked the former Minister of Personnel He Shangzhi: "Had you made Kong Xixian an Attendant Cavalier when he was nearly thirty, he would not have become a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 熙先於獄中上書曰：「囚小人猖狂，識無遠概，徒徇意氣之小感，不料逆順之大方。

translations.literal: Xixian submitted a memorial from prison: "Your prisoner, a petty man, wildly arrogant, insight lacking far-reaching scope—merely yielding to petty impulses of spirit, not calculating the broad pattern of loyalty and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian submitted a memorial from prison: "Your prisoner, a petty man, wildly arrogant, insight lacking far-reaching scope—merely yielding to petty impulses of spirit, not calculating the broad pattern of loyalty and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 與第二弟休先首為姧謀，干犯國憲，韰膾脯醢，無補尤戾。

translations.literal: With my second younger brother Xiuxian I first plotted treachery, violating the statutes of state—minced and pickled flesh would not expiate the extreme depravity.
translations.idiomatic: With my second younger brother Xiuxian I first plotted treachery, violating the statutes of state—minced and pickled flesh would not expiate such extreme depravity.

sentences.zh: 陛下大明含弘，量苞天海，錄其一介之節，猥垂優逮之詔。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, broad and tolerant, measuring to embrace sea and sky, recording a single particle of my integrity, graciously bestowed a favoring edict.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, broad and tolerant, measuring to embrace sea and sky, recording a single particle of my integrity, graciously bestowed a favoring edict.

sentences.zh: 恩非望始，沒有遺榮，終古以來，未有斯比。

translations.literal: Grace not hoped for at the beginning, at death still receiving honor—since antiquity, nothing has matched this.
translations.idiomatic: Grace not hoped for at the beginning, honor still granted at death—since antiquity, nothing has matched this.

sentences.zh: 夫盜馬絕纓之臣，懷璧投書之士，其行至賤，其過至微，由識不世之恩，以盡軀命之報，卒能立功齊、魏，致勳秦、楚。

translations.literal: The minister who stole a horse yet tied the tassel, the man who cherished his jade and cast his letter—their conduct was most base, their fault most slight—yet knowing unworldly grace, they offered their bodies in repayment, and in the end achieved merit in Qi and Wei, achievement in Qin and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The minister who stole a horse yet tied the tassel, the man who cherished his jade and cast his letter—their conduct was most base, their fault most slight—yet knowing unworldly grace, they offered their bodies in repayment, and in the end achieved merit in Qi and Wei, achievement in Qin and Chu.

sentences.zh: 囚雖身陷禍逆，名節俱喪，然少也慷慨，竊慕烈士之遺風。

translations.literal: Your prisoner, though body fallen into treason, name and integrity both lost—yet in youth I was fervent, secretly admiring the lingering style of martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: Your prisoner, though body fallen into treason and name and integrity both lost, was in youth fervent and secretly admired the lingering style of martyrs.

sentences.zh: 但墜崖之木，事絕升躋，覆盆之水，理乖收汲。

translations.literal: But wood fallen from a cliff—affairs end, no ascending; water overturning the basin—principle opposed to drawing up.
translations.idiomatic: But wood fallen from a cliff can rise no more; water spilling from an overturned basin cannot be drawn up again.

sentences.zh: 方當身膏鈇鉞，詒誡方來，若使魂而有靈，結草無遠。

translations.literal: Presently about to anoint the axe and halberd with my body, leaving admonition for those to come—if the soul has spirit, tied grass will know no distance.
translations.idiomatic: Presently about to anoint the axe and halberd with my body, leaving admonition for those to come—if the soul has spirit, tied grass will know no distance.

sentences.zh: 然區區丹抱，不負夙心，貪及視息，少得申暢。

translations.literal: Yet my petty red devotion does not betray my lifelong heart; greedy for breath still remaining, I slightly obtain expression.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my petty red devotion does not betray my lifelong heart; greedy for the breath still remaining, I slightly obtain expression.

sentences.zh: 自惟性愛群書，心解數術，智之所周，力之所至，莫不窮攬，究其幽微。

translations.literal: Reflecting that I love collecting books by nature, my heart comprehends numerology—where intelligence reaches, where strength extends, none not exhaustively gathered, probing their depths.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting that I love collecting books by nature and my heart comprehends numerology—where intelligence reaches, where strength extends, I have exhaustively gathered all and probed their depths.

sentences.zh: 考論既往，誠多審驗。

translations.literal: Examining and discussing the past, truly much verified.
translations.idiomatic: Examining and discussing the past, much has indeed been verified.

sentences.zh: 謹略陳所知，條牒如故別狀，願且勿遺棄，存之中書。

translations.literal: Respectfully I briefly set out what I know, itemized as in the separate document—I beg it not be discarded, but preserved in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully I briefly set out what I know, itemized as in the separate document. I beg it not be discarded, but preserved in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 若囚死之後，或可追存，庶九泉之下，少塞釁責。」

translations.literal: If after the prisoner's death it might be consulted and kept, perhaps under the Nine Springs I may slightly fill the gap of guilt."
translations.idiomatic: If after the prisoner's death it might be consulted and kept, perhaps under the Nine Springs I may slightly fill the gap of guilt."

sentences.zh: 所陳竝天文占候，讖上有骨肉相殘之禍，其言深切。

translations.literal: What he set out was entirely astronomical observation and omen divination—signs of flesh and bone mutually destroying within the imperial family; his words were penetratingly deep.
translations.idiomatic: What he set out was entirely astronomical observation and omen divination—signs of flesh and bone mutually destroying within the imperial family; his words were penetratingly deep.

sentences.zh: 曄在獄，與綜及熙先異處，乃稱疾求移考堂，欲近綜等。

translations.literal: Ye in prison, separately confined from Zong and Xixian, feigned illness requesting transfer to the examination hall—wishing to be near Zong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Ye in prison was separately confined from Xie Zong and Kong Xixian; he feigned illness and requested transfer to the examination hall, wishing to be near Zong and the others.

sentences.zh: 見聽，與綜等果得隔壁。

translations.literal: Permission granted—Ye indeed obtained adjoining cells with Zong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Permission was granted, and Ye indeed obtained adjoining cells with Zong and the others.

sentences.zh: 遙問綜曰：「始被收時，疑誰所告？」

translations.literal: Ye called across to ask Zong: "When first arrested, whom did you suspect informed?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye called across to ask Zong: "When first arrested, whom did you suspect had informed?"

sentences.zh: 綜云：「不知。」

translations.literal: Zong said: "I do not know."
translations.idiomatic: Zong said: "I do not know."

sentences.zh: 曄曰：「乃是徐童。」

translations.literal: Ye said: "It was Xu Tong, meaning Xu Zhanzhi."
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: "It was Xu Tong, meaning Xu Zhanzhi."

sentences.zh: 童，徐湛之小名仙童也。

translations.literal: Tong came from Xu Zhanzhi's childhood name, Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Tong came from Xu Zhanzhi's childhood name, Xiantong.

sentences.zh: 在獄為詩曰：「禍福本無兆，性命歸有極。

translations.literal: In prison he composed a poem: "Fortune and disaster originally have no omen; life and fate return to their limit.
translations.idiomatic: In prison he composed a poem: "Fortune and disaster originally have no omen; life and fate return to their limit.

sentences.zh: 必至定前期，誰能延一息。

translations.literal: The terminus must arrive at its fixed time—who can extend one breath?
translations.idiomatic: The terminus must arrive at its fixed time—who can extend one breath?

sentences.zh: 在生已可知，來緣㦎無識。

translations.literal: What is knowable in living is already knowable; karmic ties to come are obscure, without discernment.
translations.idiomatic: What may be known in this life is already knowable; the karmic ties to come are obscure beyond discernment.

sentences.zh: 好醜共一丘，何足異枉直。

translations.literal: Fair and foul share one mound—what need to distinguish crooked from straight?
translations.idiomatic: Fair and foul share one mound—what need to distinguish crooked from straight?

sentences.zh: 豈論東陵上，寧辨首山側。

translations.literal: Why discuss Dongling on the heights? Why distinguish Shoushan on the slope?
translations.idiomatic: Why discuss Dongling on the heights? Why distinguish Shoushan on the slope?

sentences.zh: 雖無嵇生琴，庶同夏侯色。

translations.literal: Though lacking Ji Kang's qin, I hope to match Xiahou's complexion.
translations.idiomatic: Though lacking Ji Kang's qin, I hope to match Xiahou's composure.

sentences.zh: 寄言生存子，此路行復即。」

translations.literal: A word to those who still live—this road you too will soon tread."
translations.idiomatic: A word to those who still live—this road you too will soon tread."

sentences.zh: 曄本意謂入獄便死，而上窮治其獄，遂經二旬，曄更有生望。

translations.literal: Ye's original intent was that entering prison meant immediate death; yet the Emperor thoroughly prosecuted the case, and after twenty days Ye again had hope of life.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's original intent was that entering prison meant immediate death; yet the Emperor thoroughly prosecuted the case, and after twenty days Ye again had hope of life.

sentences.zh: 獄吏因戲之曰：「外傳詹事或當長繫。」

translations.literal: The prison officer joked with him: "Outside it is rumored that Fan Ye, the Chamberlain, may be long imprisoned."
translations.idiomatic: The prison officer joked with him: "Outside it is rumored that Fan Ye, the Chamberlain, may be imprisoned for a long time."

sentences.zh: 曄聞之驚喜，綜、熙先笑之曰：「詹事當前共疇昔事時，無不攘袂瞋目。

translations.literal: Hearing this Ye was startled and delighted; Xie Zong and Kong Xixian laughed: "When Fan Ye, the Chamberlain, was with us plotting past affairs, never did he fail to roll up sleeves and glare.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Ye was startled and delighted. Xie Zong and Kong Xixian laughed and said: "When Fan Ye, the Chamberlain, was with us plotting those earlier affairs, never did he fail to roll up his sleeves and glare.

sentences.zh: 及在西池射堂上，躍馬顧盼，自以為一世之雄。

translations.literal: And at the West Pool archery hall, leaping on his horse and looking about, Fan Ye thought himself a hero of the age.
translations.idiomatic: And at the West Pool archery hall, leaping on his horse and looking about, Fan Ye thought himself a hero of the age.

sentences.zh: 而今擾攘紛紜，畏死乃爾。

translations.literal: Yet now, in disorder and tumult, he fears death to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now, in disorder and tumult, he fears death to this degree.

sentences.zh: 設令今時賜以性命，人臣圖主，何顏可以生存？」

translations.literal: Supposing the Emperor now granted his life—plotting against one's lord as a minister, with what face could one live?"
translations.idiomatic: Supposing the Emperor now granted his life—as a minister who plotted against his lord, with what face could one live?"

sentences.zh: 曄謂衛獄將曰：「惜哉！

translations.literal: Ye said to the prison commandant: "Pity!
translations.idiomatic: Ye said to the prison commandant: "What a pity!

sentences.zh: 薶如此人。」

translations.literal: To bury such a man."
translations.idiomatic: To bury such a man."

sentences.zh: 將曰：「不忠之人，亦何足惜。」

translations.literal: The commandant said: "A disloyal man—what is there to pity?"
translations.idiomatic: The commandant said: "A disloyal man—what is there to pity?"

sentences.zh: 曄曰：「大將言是也。」

translations.literal: Ye said: "The General speaks correctly."
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: "The General speaks correctly."

sentences.zh: 將出市，曄最在前，於獄門顧謂綜曰：「今日次第，當以位邪？」

translations.literal: When led out to execution, Ye was foremost; at the prison gate he looked back at Zong: "Today's order—should it follow rank?"
translations.idiomatic: When led out to execution, Ye was foremost. At the prison gate he looked back at Zong and said: "Today's order—should it follow rank?"

sentences.zh: 綜曰：「賊帥為先。」

translations.literal: Zong said: "The rebel chief goes first."
translations.idiomatic: Zong said: "The rebel chief goes first."

sentences.zh: 在道語笑，初無暫止。

translations.literal: Along the way they talked and laughed without pause.
translations.idiomatic: Along the way they talked and laughed without pause.

sentences.zh: 至市，問綜曰：「時欲至未？」

translations.literal: Reaching the market, he asked Zong: "Has the hour nearly come?"
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the market, he asked Zong: "Has the hour nearly come?"

sentences.zh: 綜曰：「勢不復久。」

translations.literal: Zong said: "It surely will not be long."
translations.idiomatic: Zong said: "It surely will not be long."

sentences.zh: 曄既食，又苦勸綜，綜曰：「此異病篤，何事強飯。」

translations.literal: After Ye had eaten, he earnestly urged Zong to eat; Zong said: "For this strange illness, what need to force food?"
translations.idiomatic: After Ye had eaten, he earnestly urged Zong to eat. Zong said: "For this strange illness, what need to force food?"

sentences.zh: 曄家人悉至市，監刑職司問：「須相見不？」

translations.literal: Ye's family all arrived at the market; the execution supervisor asked: "Do you wish to see them?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye's family all arrived at the market. The execution supervisor asked: "Do you wish to see them?"

sentences.zh: 曄問綜曰：「家人以來，幸得相見，將不踅別。」

translations.literal: Ye asked Zong: "Family has come—I am fortunate to see them; I will not turn back for farewell."
translations.idiomatic: Ye asked Zong: "Family has come—I am fortunate to see them. I will not turn back for farewell."

sentences.zh: 綜曰：「別與不別，亦何所存。

translations.literal: Zong said: "Farewell or not—what does it matter?
translations.idiomatic: Zong said: "Farewell or not—what does it matter?

sentences.zh: 來必當號泣，正足亂人意。」

translations.literal: They will surely wail and weep—just enough to unsettle the mind."
translations.idiomatic: They will surely wail and weep—just enough to unsettle the mind."

sentences.zh: 曄曰：「號泣何關人，向見道邊親故相瞻望，亦殊勝不見。

translations.literal: Ye said: "Weeping concerns no one else; earlier I saw relatives and old friends on the roadside gazing over—that too was splendid, better than not seeing.
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: "Weeping concerns no one else. Earlier I saw relatives and old friends on the roadside gazing over—that too was splendid, better than not seeing.

sentences.zh: 吾意故欲相見。」

translations.literal: My intention from the start has been to see them."
translations.idiomatic: I have always meant to see them."

sentences.zh: 於是呼前。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had them called forward.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he had them called forward.

sentences.zh: 曄妻先下撫其子，回罵曄曰：「君不為百歲阿家，不感天子恩遇，身死固不足塞罪，奈何枉殺子孫。」

translations.literal: Ye's wife came down first and stroked her child; turning back she cursed Ye, saying: "You do not think of your aged mother-in-law who may live a hundred years, you feel no gratitude for the Son of Heaven's grace and favor—death by itself surely cannot atone for the crime; why must you wrongfully kill our children and descendants?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye's wife came down first and comforted her child, then turned and cursed Ye: "You spare no thought for your aged mother-in-law, you show no gratitude for the emperor's grace and favor—your death alone could never atone for this crime, so why must you wrongfully destroy our children and descendants?"

sentences.zh: 曄乾笑云罪至而已。

translations.literal: Ye gave a dry laugh and said the crime had simply run its course.
translations.idiomatic: Ye gave a dry laugh and said only that punishment had come due.

sentences.zh: 曄所生母泣曰：「主上念汝無極，汝曾不能感恩，又不念我老，今日奈何？」

translations.literal: Ye's biological mother wept and said: "The sovereign thinks of you beyond measure; you cannot even be grateful, nor consider my old age—what of today?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye's birth mother wept and said: "The sovereign has shown you boundless favor; you cannot even be grateful, nor spare a thought for my old age—what is to become of today?"

sentences.zh: 仍以手擊曄頸及頰，曄顏色不怍。

translations.literal: Still she struck Ye's neck and cheeks with her hands; Ye's expression showed no shame.
translations.idiomatic: She still struck Ye's neck and cheeks with her hands, yet Ye's face showed no shame.

sentences.zh: 妻云：「罪人，阿家莫念。」

translations.literal: His wife said: "A guilty man—mother-in-law, do not dwell on it."
translations.idiomatic: His wife said: "I am the guilty one—mother-in-law, do not grieve over this."

sentences.zh: 妹及妓妾來別，曄悲涕流漣，綜曰：「舅殊不同夏侯色。」

translations.literal: His sisters and concubines came to bid farewell; Ye wept with flowing tears; Zong said: "Uncle, you are quite unlike Xiahou's composure."
translations.idiomatic: His sisters and concubines came to say farewell. Ye wept with tears streaming down. Zong said: "Uncle, you are nothing like Xiahou's composure."

sentences.zh: 曄收淚而止。

translations.literal: Ye wiped his tears and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ye wiped away his tears and stopped.

sentences.zh: 綜母以子弟自蹈逆亂，獨不出視。

translations.literal: Zong's mother, because her sons and younger brothers had themselves plunged into rebellion, alone did not come out to look.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's mother, because her sons and younger brothers had themselves plunged into treason, alone refused to come out and look.

sentences.zh: 曄語綜曰：「姊今不來，勝人多也。」

translations.literal: Ye said to Zong: "If elder sister does not come today, that is better than many people."
translations.idiomatic: Ye said to Zong: "If my elder sister does not come today, that is better than a crowd of people."

sentences.zh: 曄轉醉，子藹亦醉，取地土及果皮以擲曄，呼曄為別駕數十聲。

translations.literal: Ye grew increasingly drunk; his son Fan Ai, also drunk, took earth and fruit peels to throw at Ye, calling Ye "Assistant Administrator" dozens of times.
translations.idiomatic: Ye grew still more drunk. His son Fan Ai, also drunk, picked up dirt and fruit peels and threw them at Ye, calling him "Assistant Administrator" dozens of times.

sentences.zh: 曄問曰：「汝恚我邪？」

translations.literal: Ye asked: "Are you angry at me?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye asked: "Are you angry at me?"

sentences.zh: 藹曰：「今日何緣復恚？

translations.literal: Fan Ai said: "What cause today to be angry again?
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ai said: "What reason is there to be angry today?

sentences.zh: 但父子同死，不能不悲耳。」

translations.literal: Only that father and son die together—cannot but grieve, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Only that father and son die together — that is what grieves me."

sentences.zh: 曄常謂死者神滅，欲著《無鬼論》；

translations.literal: Ye had often said that when the dead die their spirits are extinguished, and wished to write On the Nonexistence of Ghosts;
translations.idiomatic: Ye had often maintained that the dead leave no surviving spirit and had wished to write On the Nonexistence of Ghosts;

sentences.zh: 至是與徐湛之書，云「當相訟地下」。

translations.literal: at this time in a letter to Xu Zhanzhi he wrote, "We shall sue each other in the underworld."
translations.idiomatic: yet now in a letter to Xu Zhanzhi he wrote, "We shall bring suit against each other in the underworld."

sentences.zh: 其謬亂如此。

translations.literal: His confusion and contradiction were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: His self-contradiction was as absurd as this.

sentences.zh: 又語人：「寄語何僕射，天下決無佛鬼。

translations.literal: He also told people: "Send word to Vice Director He: Under Heaven there are absolutely no Buddhas or ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: He also told others: "Send word to Vice Director He: there are absolutely no Buddhas or ghosts in this world.

sentences.zh: 若有靈，自當相報。」

translations.literal: If they exist with spiritual power, they will surely repay in kind."
translations.idiomatic: If they truly have power, they will surely settle accounts with me."

sentences.zh: 收曄家，樂器服玩，並皆珍麗，妓妾亦盛飾，母住止單陋，唯有一廚盛樵薪，弟子冬無被，叔父單布衣。

translations.literal: When Ye's property was confiscated: musical instruments, apparel, and playthings were all precious and splendid; concubines also splendidly adorned; his mother lived in bare simplicity, with only one kitchen storing firewood; younger brother's sons had no quilts in winter; his uncle wore only plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye's household was searched and confiscated, his musical instruments, clothing, and curios were all precious and splendid, and his concubines were richly adorned; yet his mother lived in bare poverty, with only one kitchen stacked with firewood, his younger brother's sons had no quilts in winter, and his uncle wore only a single layer of plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 曄及子藹、遙、叔蔞、孔熙先及弟休先、景先、思先、熙先子桂甫、桂甫子白民、謝綜及弟約、仲承祖、許耀，諸所連及，並伏誅。

translations.literal: Fan Ye and his sons Fan Ai, Fan Yao, and Fan Shusou; Kong Xixian and his younger brothers Kong Xiuxian, Kong Jingxian, and Kong Sixian; Xixian's son Kong Guifu and Guifu's son Kong Baimin; Xie Zong and his younger brother Xie Yue; Zhong Chengzu; and Xu Yao—all those implicated were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye and his sons Fan Ai, Fan Yao, and Fan Shusou; Kong Xixian and his younger brothers Kong Xiuxian, Kong Jingxian, and Kong Sixian; Xixian's son Kong Guifu and Guifu's son Kong Baimin; Xie Zong and his younger brother Xie Yue; Zhong Chengzu; and Xu Yao—all those implicated were put to death.

sentences.zh: 曄時年四十八。

translations.literal: Ye was then forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was forty-eight at the time.

sentences.zh: 曄兄弟子父已亡者及謝綜弟緯，徙廣州。

translations.literal: Ye's brothers' sons whose fathers had already died, and Xie Zong's younger brother Wei, were exiled to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Ye's brothers whose fathers were already dead, together with Xie Zong's younger brother Wei, were exiled to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 藹子魯連，吳興昭公主外孫，請全生命，亦得遠徙，世祖即位得還。

translations.literal: Fan Ai's son Lulian, grandson of Princess Zhao of Wuxing, pleaded to spare his life; he too was exiled afar; when Shizu ascended the throne he was allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ai's son Lulian, a grandson of Princess Zhao of Wuxing, pleaded for his life and was likewise exiled to a distant place; when Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, he was permitted to return.

sentences.zh: 曄性精微，有思致，觸類多善，衣裳器服，莫不增損制度，世人皆法學之。

translations.literal: Ye's nature was subtle and refined, with thoughtful ideas; in every category he excelled at many things; clothing, utensils, and attire—none without additions or alterations to design; worldly people all modeled themselves on and studied him.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's nature was subtle and refined, full of thoughtful invention; he excelled in one thing after another, and in clothing, utensils, and dress he altered and improved every design, so that people everywhere copied and studied his ways.

sentences.zh: 撰《和香方》，其序之曰：「麝本多忌，過分必害；

translations.literal: He compiled Formulas for Blending Incense, and in its preface wrote: "Musk by nature has many taboos—exceed the proper measure and it must harm;
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Formulas for Blending Incense, and in its preface wrote: "Musk by nature has many taboos—use too much and it turns harmful;

sentences.zh: 沈實易和，盈斤無傷。

translations.literal: dark resin is easy to harmonize—a full jin does no injury.
translations.idiomatic: dark resin blends easily—even a full jin does no harm.

sentences.zh: 零藿虛燥，詹唐黏濕。

translations.literal: Zerumbet is hollow and dry; sweet flag is sticky and damp.
translations.idiomatic: Zerumbet is hollow and dry; sweet flag is sticky and damp.

sentences.zh: 甘松、蘇合、安息、鬱金、㮏多、和羅之屬，並被珍於外國，無取於中土。

translations.literal: Types such as spikenard, storax, benzoin, turmeric, naiduo, and heluo are all treasured in foreign lands and not sought in the central land.
translations.idiomatic: Spikenard, storax, benzoin, turmeric, naiduo, heluo, and the like are all prized in foreign lands and have no place in the central realm.

sentences.zh: 又棗膏昏鈍，甲煎淺俗，非唯無助於馨烈，乃當彌增於尤疾也。」

translations.literal: Again, jujube paste is dull and obtuse, and cassia decoction is shallow and vulgar—they not only fail to aid fragrance and strength but will only increase serious faults."
translations.idiomatic: Jujube paste is dull and heavy, and cassia decoction is shallow and vulgar—they not only fail to enhance fragrance and potency but only deepen serious flaws."

sentences.zh: 此序所言，悉以比類朝士：「麝本多忌」，比庾炳之；

translations.literal: All that this preface says was entirely used to compare court gentlemen by category: "Musk by nature has many taboos" compared Yu Bingzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Everything in this preface was in fact an allegory for court gentlemen: "Musk by nature has many taboos" referred to Yu Bingzhi;

sentences.zh: 「零藿虛燥」，比何尚之；

translations.literal: "Zerumbet is hollow and dry" compared He Shangzhi;
translations.idiomatic: "Zerumbet is hollow and dry" referred to He Shangzhi;

sentences.zh: 「詹唐黏濕」，比沈演之；

translations.literal: "Sweet flag is sticky and damp" compared Shen Yanzhi;
translations.idiomatic: "Sweet flag is sticky and damp" referred to Shen Yanzhi;

sentences.zh: 「棗膏昏鈍」，比羊玄保；

translations.literal: "Jujube paste is dull and obtuse" compared Yang Xuanbao;
translations.idiomatic: "Jujube paste is dull and obtuse" referred to Yang Xuanbao;

sentences.zh: 「甲煎淺俗」，比徐湛之；

translations.literal: "Cassia decoction is shallow and vulgar" compared Xu Zhanzhi;
translations.idiomatic: "Cassia decoction is shallow and vulgar" referred to Xu Zhanzhi;

sentences.zh: 「甘松、蘇合」，比慧琳道人；

translations.literal: "Spikenard and storax" compared the monk Huilin;
translations.idiomatic: "Spikenard and storax" referred to the monk Huilin;

sentences.zh: 「沈實易和」，以自比也。

translations.literal: "Dark resin is easy to harmonize"—he compared himself.
translations.idiomatic: "Dark resin blends easily"—that was his self-comparison.

sentences.zh: 曄獄中與諸甥姪書以自序曰：

translations.literal: In prison Ye wrote a self-preface in a letter to his nephews, saying:
translations.idiomatic: From prison Ye wrote a self-preface in a letter to his nephews, saying:

sentences.zh: 吾狂釁覆滅，豈復可言，汝等皆當以罪人棄之。

translations.literal: My mad outrage has brought total ruin—what more can be said; you all should cast me off as a criminal.
translations.idiomatic: My reckless crime has brought utter ruin—there is nothing more to say. You should all cast me off as a criminal.

sentences.zh: 然平生行己任懷，猶應可尋。

translations.literal: Yet my conduct and bearing in life should still be traceable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the way I lived and what I held in my heart should still be worth tracing.

sentences.zh: 至於能不，意中所解，汝等或不悉知。

translations.literal: As for what I can and cannot do, and what my mind understands—you may not fully know.
translations.idiomatic: As for what I could and could not do, and what I understood in my mind—you may not know it all.

sentences.zh: 吾少懶學問，晚成人，年三十許，政始有向耳。

translations.literal: I was lazy in study when young and matured late; around thirty I only then began to have direction.
translations.idiomatic: I was lazy about learning in youth and came to maturity late; only around thirty did I begin to find my direction.

sentences.zh: 自爾以來，轉為心化，推老將至者，亦當未已也。

translations.literal: Since then my heart has gradually transformed; I reckon that even approaching old age, this will not yet have ceased.
translations.idiomatic: From then on my heart kept changing for the better; I expect that even as old age draws near, this will not yet have stopped.

sentences.zh: 往往有微解，言乃不能自盡。

translations.literal: Often I had partial understanding, yet words could not fully express it.
translations.idiomatic: I often grasped things in part, yet could never fully express them in words.

sentences.zh: 為性不尋注書，心氣惡，小苦思，便憒悶；

translations.literal: By nature I do not pore over books; my heart and spirit are troubled—slight painful thinking and I grow restless and distressed;
translations.idiomatic: By nature I could not fix my mind on books; my heart and spirit were ill at ease—after even a little strenuous thought I grew restless and oppressed;

sentences.zh: 口機又不調利，以此無談功。

translations.literal: my tongue and wit were not agile, hence I had no triumph in discourse.
translations.idiomatic: my tongue and wit were not nimble, and so I had no gift for debate.

sentences.zh: 至於所通解處，皆自得之於胸懷耳。

translations.literal: What I did grasp and understand, I attained entirely within my own breast.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever I did understand, I arrived at entirely within my own breast.

sentences.zh: 文章轉進，但才少思難，所以每於操筆，其所成篇，殆無全稱者。

translations.literal: My writing steadily improved, but talent was slight and thinking difficult; therefore whenever I took up the brush, scarcely any finished piece won full praise.
translations.idiomatic: My writing improved steadily, but my talent was limited and thinking came hard; so whenever I wrote, scarcely any finished piece won full praise.

sentences.zh: 常恥作文士。

translations.literal: I was always ashamed to be a literary artisan.
translations.idiomatic: I was always ashamed to be counted among literary craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 文患其事盡於形，情急於藻，義牽其旨，韻移其意。

translations.literal: Writing's fault is that events exhaust themselves in form, feeling rushes to ornament, meaning is dragged by its theme, and rhyme shifts its intent.
translations.idiomatic: The fault of writing is that events are spent entirely on surface form, feeling hurries into ornament, meaning is pulled about by theme, and rhyme displaces intent.

sentences.zh: 雖時有能者，大較多不免此累，政可類工巧圖繢，竟無得也。

translations.literal: Though sometimes there are able ones, most cannot escape this burden—it is just like the craft of decorative painting, ultimately achieving nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Though there are occasionally able writers, most cannot escape this failing—it is like decorative painting: in the end nothing is truly gained.

sentences.zh: 常謂情志所託，故當以意為主，以文傳意。

translations.literal: I always said that since feeling and intent are what writing entrusts, one should take meaning as master and use words to convey meaning.
translations.idiomatic: I always held that since writing exists to carry feeling and intent, meaning should be master and words should transmit meaning.

sentences.zh: 以意為主，則其旨必見；

translations.literal: When meaning is master, its point must appear;
translations.idiomatic: When meaning is master, the point must show through;

sentences.zh: 以文傳意，則其詞不流。

translations.literal: when words transmit meaning, the language does not run loose.
translations.idiomatic: when words transmit meaning, the language does not run away.

sentences.zh: 然後抽其芬芳，振其金石耳。

translations.literal: Only then may one draw out fragrance and strike the metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Only then can one draw out fragrance and strike notes like metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 此中情性旨趣，千條百品，屈曲有成理。

translations.literal: Within this, emotional nature and intent have a thousand strands and a hundred kinds, winding and turning yet forming a pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Within this, the turns of feeling and intent come in countless varieties, winding yet forming their own logic.

sentences.zh: 自謂頗識其數，嘗為人言，多不能賞，意或異故也。

translations.literal: I thought myself fairly to know their number; when I once spoke of them to others, most could not appreciate it—perhaps because their intent differed.
translations.idiomatic: I believed I understood this fairly well; when I spoke of it to others, most could not appreciate it—perhaps because their minds ran another way.

sentences.zh: 性別宮商，識清濁，斯自然也。

translations.literal: By nature to distinguish gong from shang and to know clear from muddy—this is natural.
translations.idiomatic: To distinguish gong from shang by nature and to know clear from muddy tones—this is innate.

sentences.zh: 觀古今文人，多不全了此處，縱有會此者，不必從根本中來。

translations.literal: Looking at writers ancient and modern, most do not fully grasp this point; even those who sometimes understand it need not have come to it from the root.
translations.idiomatic: Looking at writers ancient and modern, most do not fully grasp this; even those who sometimes understand it need not have reached it from the root.

sentences.zh: 言之皆有實證，非為空談。

translations.literal: What I say all has real proof—it is not empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: What I say rests on real evidence—it is not empty talk.

sentences.zh: 年少中，謝莊最有其分，手筆差易，文不拘韻故也。

translations.literal: Among the young, Xie Zhuang had the greatest share of this gift; his hand moved rather easily, because his writing was not bound by rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: Among younger writers, Xie Zhuang possessed this gift most fully; his pen moved rather easily because his writing was not bound by rhyme.

sentences.zh: 吾思乃無定方，特能濟難適輕重，所稟之分，猶當未盡。

translations.literal: My thinking has no fixed method; I am only especially able to meet difficulty and suit light and heavy—the share of gift I received is probably not yet exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: My thinking has no fixed method; I am only especially able to meet difficulty and adjust weight and lightness—the measure of gift I was born with is probably not yet exhausted.

sentences.zh: 但多公家之言，少於事外遠致，以此為恨，亦由無意於文名故也。

translations.literal: But there is much language of public office and little reaching beyond affairs to distant effect—this I regret, and it is also because I had no wish for literary fame.
translations.idiomatic: But my writing is mostly the language of public office, with little reach beyond affairs into distant resonance—this I regret, and it is also because I cared nothing for literary fame.

sentences.zh: 本未關史書，政恆覺其不可解耳。

translations.literal: Originally I had no connection with historical books; I always simply felt them incomprehensible.
translations.idiomatic: At first I had nothing to do with historical books; I always found them simply incomprehensible.

sentences.zh: 既造《後漢》，轉得統緒，詳觀古今著述及評論，殆少可意者。

translations.literal: Once I undertook the Later Han, I gradually gained its thread; closely observing writings and commentaries ancient and modern, scarcely any pleased me.
translations.idiomatic: Once I undertook the History of the Later Han, I gradually grasped its thread; surveying writings and commentaries ancient and modern, scarcely any satisfied me.

sentences.zh: 班氏最有高名，既任情無例，不可甲乙辨。

translations.literal: The Ban clan has the highest fame, yet indulges feeling without rule—it cannot be ranked first or second for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: The Ban clan enjoys the highest fame, yet writes at whim without consistent rule—it cannot be ranked for clear comparison.

sentences.zh: 後贊於理近無所得，唯志可推耳。

translations.literal: The later encomia gain little in principle; only the Treatises can be commended.
translations.idiomatic: Their later encomia yield little in principle; only the Treatises are truly admirable.

sentences.zh: 博贍不可及之，整理未必愧也。

translations.literal: In breadth and sufficiency one cannot reach them; in ordering and arrangement one need not feel ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: In breadth and comprehensiveness one cannot match them; in ordering and arrangement one need not feel ashamed.

sentences.zh: 吾雜傳論，皆有精意深旨，既有裁味，故約其詞句。

translations.literal: My assorted biography commentaries all have refined meaning and deep intent; since they already have restrained flavor, I therefore condensed their wording.
translations.idiomatic: My assorted biography commentaries all carry refined meaning and deep intent; because they already have restrained flavor, I therefore kept their wording spare.

sentences.zh: 至於《循吏》以下及《六夷》諸序論，筆勢縱放，實天下之奇作。

translations.literal: As for those from Diligent Officials downward and the prefaces and commentaries on the Six Barbarians, the brush momentum is unrestrained—they are truly wondrous works under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: As for those from Diligent Officials downward and the prefaces and commentaries on the Six Barbarians, the brush runs free—they are truly wondrous works under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其中合者，往往不減《過秦》篇。

translations.literal: Those among them that succeed often do not fall short of the essay "Faults of Qin."
translations.idiomatic: Those among them that succeed often do not fall short of Jia Yi's "Faults of Qin."

sentences.zh: 嘗共比方班氏所作，非但不愧之而已。

translations.literal: I once compared them with the Ban clan's work—not only without shame but more.
translations.idiomatic: I once compared them with the Ban clan's work—not only without shame, but more than that.

sentences.zh: 欲遍作諸志，前漢所有者悉令備。

translations.literal: I wished to compose all the Treatises in full, making complete whatever the Former Han possessed.
translations.idiomatic: I intended to write all the Treatises in full, completing whatever the Former Han History contained.

sentences.zh: 雖事不必多，且使見文得盡。

translations.literal: Though the matters need not be many, I wished at least to let the text be seen in full.
translations.idiomatic: Though the entries need not be numerous, I wanted at least to let the text appear complete.

sentences.zh: 又欲因事就卷內發論，以正一代得失，意復未果。

translations.literal: I also wished, according to events, to set forth commentaries within the scrolls to rectify a generation's gains and losses—but that intent again did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: I also wished to develop commentaries within each scroll according to the events, to judge a generation's gains and losses—but that intent too remained unrealized.

sentences.zh: 贊自是吾文之傑思，殆無一字空設，奇變不窮，同合異體，乃自不知所以稱之。

translations.literal: The encomia are truly the outstanding thought of my writing— scarcely a word is set in vain; strange transformations are inexhaustible, same in fusion yet different in form—I myself do not know how to name them.
translations.idiomatic: The encomia are truly the outstanding achievement of my writing—hardly a word is empty; their strange transformations are inexhaustible, unified yet diverse in form—I myself hardly know how to describe them.

sentences.zh: 此書行，故應有賞音者。

translations.literal: When this book circulates, there should be those who appreciate its tone.
translations.idiomatic: When this book goes abroad, there should be readers who appreciate its tone.

sentences.zh: 紀、傳例為舉其大略耳，諸細意甚多。

translations.literal: The Annals and Biographies sections only set forth the broad outline; the finer points are very many.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals and Biographies sections only give the broad outline; the finer points are very numerous.

sentences.zh: 自古體大而思精，未有此也。

translations.literal: From antiquity, none has been so large in form and so refined in thought as this.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity onward, nothing has been so large in scope and so refined in thought as this.

sentences.zh: 恐世人不能盡之，多貴古賤今，所以稱情狂言耳。

translations.literal: I fear the world cannot fully grasp it; most honor the ancient and despise the present—therefore these words spoken from the heart are bold talk.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the world will not fully grasp it; most people honor the ancient and despise the present—therefore these heartfelt words are bold speech.

sentences.zh: 吾於音樂，聽功不及自揮，但所精非雅聲，為可恨。

translations.literal: In music, my power of listening did not match my power of playing—but what I mastered was not elegant sound, which is regrettable.
translations.idiomatic: In music, my ear was not the equal of my hand—but what I mastered was not refined court music, which I regret.

sentences.zh: 然至於一絕處，亦復何異邪！

translations.literal: Yet at the point of absolute mastery, what difference is there!
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the point of absolute mastery, what difference does it make!

sentences.zh: 其中體趣，言之不盡，弦外之意，虛響之音，不知所從而來。

translations.literal: The inner tone within cannot be fully spoken; meaning beyond the strings, empty reverberating sound—I do not know whence it comes.
translations.idiomatic: Its inner tone cannot be fully expressed; meaning beyond the strings, empty reverberating sound—I do not know whence it comes.

sentences.zh: 雖少許處，而旨態無極。

translations.literal: Though in only a few places, the intent and bearing are boundless.
translations.idiomatic: Though it appears in only a few places, its intent and bearing are boundless.

sentences.zh: 亦嘗以授人，士庶中未有一毫似者。

translations.literal: I also once taught it to others, but among gentlemen and commoners not one showed the slightest likeness.
translations.idiomatic: I also once taught it to others, but among gentlemen and commoners not one resembled it in the slightest.

sentences.zh: 此永不傳矣。

translations.literal: This will never be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: This will never be handed down.

sentences.zh: 吾書雖小小有意，筆勢不快，餘竟不成就，每愧此名。

translations.literal: My calligraphy, though it has a little intent, lacks swift brush momentum; the rest never came to completion—I always feel ashamed of this name.
translations.idiomatic: My calligraphy, though it has a little intention, lacks swift brush momentum; the rest never came to fruition—I always feel ashamed of this reputation.

sentences.zh: 曄《自序》並實，故存之。

translations.literal: Ye's Self-Preface is factual, therefore it is preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's Self-Preface is factual, and so it is preserved here.

sentences.zh: 藹幼而整潔，衣服竟歲未嘗有塵點。

translations.literal: Fan Ai from youth was neat and clean; his clothes throughout the year never once had a speck of dust.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ai was neat and orderly from childhood; his clothes went a whole year without a speck of dust.

sentences.zh: 死時年二十。

translations.literal: At death Fan Ai was twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ai was twenty when he died.

sentences.zh: 曄少時，兄晏常云：「此兒進利，終破門戶。」

translations.literal: When Ye was young, elder brother Yan often said: "This boy seeks profit—he will in the end destroy the family."
translations.idiomatic: When Ye was young, his elder brother Yan often said: "This boy is greedy for gain—he will destroy the family in the end."

sentences.zh: 終如晏言。

translations.literal: In the end it was as Yan said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it happened just as Yan said.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：古之人云：「利令智昏。」

translations.literal: The historian writes: The ancients said: "Profit makes the mind dull."
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The ancients said, "Profit makes the mind dull."

sentences.zh: 甚矣，利害之相傾。

translations.literal: How extreme is the mutual overthrow of benefit and harm!
translations.idiomatic: How extreme is the way benefit and harm overturn one another!

sentences.zh: 劉湛識用才能，實苞經國之略，豈不知移弟為臣，則君臣之道用；

translations.literal: Liu Zhan in insight and employment of talent truly embraced the strategy to govern a state—how could he not know that if a younger brother becomes a subject, then the way of ruler and minister applies;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan's insight and talent truly encompassed the strategy to govern a state—how could he not know that when a younger brother becomes a subject, the way of ruler and minister applies;

sentences.zh: 變兄成主，則兄弟之義殊乎？

translations.literal: if an elder brother becomes a lord, then the righteousness of brothers is altered?
translations.idiomatic: and when an elder brother becomes a sovereign, the bond between brothers is altered?

sentences.zh: 而義康數懷姧計，苟相崇說，與夫推長戟而犯魏闕，亦何以異哉！

translations.literal: Yet Yikang repeatedly harbored treacherous designs, and if one exalts and urges him on, what difference is there from pushing a long halberd to assault the palace gate!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yikang repeatedly harbored treacherous designs, and to exalt and urge him on—how is that different from pushing a long halberd against the palace gate!
